docs.title: Chosen of the Harvest
docs.text:
A complete, code-driven action-roguelike + sanctuary-management framework for Unity 6 — ready to reskin and ship.

Chosen of the Harvest is a production-ready Unity template: you build a sanctuary, recruit and manage a cast of followers, then descend into repeatable expeditions to break the Wardens who hoard the harvest. Every system is written in C# and generated at runtime, so there is no prefab wiring to maintain and no scene to repair — reskin the art, retune the numbers, and it is your game.

  • :material-rocket-launch: Runs out of the box

    Open the project, press Play. The hub, the followers, the HUD, the dungeon and the bosses assemble themselves from code.

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Your first run

  • :material-palette: Built to reskin

    All presentation flows through catalogs and Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Resources, so replacing art, audio and copy never touches gameplay logic.

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Customization

  • :material-cube-outline: Systems, not a demo

    Save slots with migration and backup recovery, procedural floors, a follower simulation with needs and jobs, quests, meta-progression and localisation.

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Architecture

  • :material-bookshelf: Documented

    Every system has a guide page, and the public API surface is catalogued in the reference section.

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Reference

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Before you start

  • Unity 6000.6.6f1 or newer Unity 6 release (earlier Unity 6 releases will prompt an upgrade).
  • Input System and Universal Render Pipeline packages — both are already declared in Packages/manifest.json.
  • No third-party assets, plugins or paid dependencies. Everything included is generated in-house and covered by the template licence.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to the Chosen of the Harvest template are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the package uses Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: [1.0.0] — 2026-10-22
docs.text: First public release.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Code-driven architecture. One scene, one entry point. HarvestGame builds the camera, hub, player, companions, HUD and audio at runtime; there are no prefabs or scene references.
  • Sanctuary management. 20 sanctum types with levels, condition, dirt, workers, production, repairs and player-built interiors (walls, doors, decor).
  • Follower simulation. Needs, hunger, loyalty, exhaustion, sickness, traits, jobs, priorities, beds, relationships, children, memorials and death.
  • Expeditions. Procedural floor plans across 3 acts / 6 floors / 92 rooms, with keys, shops, treasure, puzzles, curses and corridors.
  • Combat. 12 armaments, 3 rites, bombs, dodge with i-frames, bleed/slow/burn/poison, 12 creature archetypes and 3 elite modifiers.
  • Three Wardens with unique arenas, phases, Ascendant forms and deaths.
  • Progression. 18 omens, 18 heirlooms, 11 attire pieces, devotion meta-upgrades and a 9-stage quest chain.
  • Persistence. Save schema 4, three manual slots plus autosave, atomic writes, .bak recovery and a migration/repair pass.
  • Presentation. Code-built uGUI HUD, photo mode, settings (volume, difficulty, UI scale, high contrast, reduced motion, FPS counter, autosave), key rebinding and mute.
  • Localisation. 349 keys, English plus a pseudo-locale for layout testing, with runtime hot switching.
  • Content. 49 placeholder sprites and 21 placeholder audio clips, all loaded by path and replaceable without code changes.
  • Editor tooling. Scene builder, standalone player builders for Windows, Linux and macOS, and an AssetPostprocessor that enforces sprite import rules.
  • Verification. A -smoke pass that exercises the whole game loop, plus Tools/build.ps1 -RunSmoke.
  • Documentation. Offline manual in Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Documentation/ and this online site.
  • Compliance files. Third-Party Notices.txt and AI-Disclosure.md.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Editor menu moved under Tools → Chosen of the Harvest to match Asset Store packaging rules.
  • Build logs are written to BuildLogs/ only; the player output folder contains no text files.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Static runtime state is reset on subsystem registration, so the template supports Fast Enter Playmode with Domain Reload disabled (Unity 6.6+).
  • Time.timeScale is now derived every frame from the pause, photo-mode and hit-stop state, so an overlapping hit-stop can no longer leave the game frozen.
  • Replaced deprecated FindObjectsByType(FindObjectsSortMode) and FindFirstObjectByType calls with their current Unity 6 equivalents, removing all obsolete-API compiler warnings.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Rendering is 2D sprites in a 3D stage; there are no 3D character models.
  • Combat is keyboard/gamepad only — there is no click-to-move.
  • The catalogs are plain C# arrays, not ScriptableObject assets.
  • Art and audio are placeholders; expect to replace them before shipping.

docs.title: Is this a finished game?
docs.text: No. It is a template: a complete, playable framework you reskin and extend. The included art and audio are placeholders, and the lore names are deliberately generic so you can replace them.

docs.title: Which Unity version do I need?
docs.text: 6000.6.6f1 (Unity 6) or a newer Unity 6 release. Unity 2022.3 and earlier are not supported.

docs.title: Does it need URP?
docs.text: Yes. The project uses the Universal Render Pipeline with the 2D renderer. HDRP is not supported out of the box.

docs.title: Are there prefabs I can edit?
docs.text: No. The template generates everything at runtime from code, which is why it cannot break from missing references. If you prefer prefabs, the catalogs are plain serializable classes and can be moved to ScriptableObjects.

docs.title: Can I use this in a commercial game?
docs.text: Yes. The package is distributed under the Unity Asset Store EULA. You can ship games built with it. You cannot resell or redistribute the template itself.

docs.title: Is the art AI-generated?
docs.text: The 49 sprites are AI-generated and disclosed in AI disclosure. The 21 audio clips are synthesised procedurally by the project's own code.

docs.title: Why is there no music track I recognise?
docs.text: There is no third-party audio. Every clip is original.

docs.title: The scene is empty when I press Play
docs.text: You opened the wrong scene. Open Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Scenes/ChosenOfTheHarvest.unity. If that file is missing, run Tools → Chosen of the Harvest → Create or Repair Bootstrap Scene.

docs.title: Everything is pink
docs.text: The URP pipeline asset is not assigned. Open Project Settings → Graphics and set Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Settings/UniversalRP.asset as the default pipeline asset, and the same file in Quality.

docs.title: error CS0234: The type or namespace name 'InputSystem' does not exist
docs.text: The Input System package did not resolve. Open Window → Package Manager → In Project and install/reinstall Input System, then let Unity restart.

docs.title: Can I open it in Unity 6000.5?
docs.text: It may work, but the package targets 6000.6.6f1 and is tested there. Downgrades are not supported by Unity.

docs.title: Does it work with Domain Reload disabled?
docs.text: Yes. Fast Enter Playmode is supported: every static field is reset on subsystem registration. See Architecture.

docs.title: How do I get more companions?
docs.text: Rescue them from the Fallow, or recruit from the generated pool. The cap is 30. Beds raise the comfortable population.

docs.title: My companions keep starving
docs.text: Build a Rose Garden and assign a worker, or hold a Hymn (it feeds one food per companion). A Kitchen Pavilion lowers the feast cost from 8 to 4 food.

docs.title: How do I cure a sick companion?
docs.text: Build an Elixir Atelier to make medicine, or hold the Ceremony of Warding (10 pearls) to cure everyone at once.

docs.title: Where do pearls come from?
docs.text: Combat kills, chests, boss rewards and the Sacrifice ceremony.

docs.title: How do I unlock Act II?
docs.text: Defeat the Act I Warden, The Gilded Stag, in the Ashen Orchard.

docs.title: How do I get devotion?
docs.text: Quests (2–4 per stage), bosses (8/12/16), pilgrimages, and the Sovereign's Diadem heirloom.

docs.title: The build menu is missing a building
docs.text: Some buildings unlock by campaign progress or require resources you do not have. Check the cost line — the menu greys out unaffordable entries.

docs.title: Can I play with a controller?
docs.text: Yes. See Controls.

docs.title: How do I rename the game?
docs.text: Project Settings → Player → Product Name and Company Name, then update HarvestGame.Version and the en.json title keys. See Rebranding the template.

docs.title: How do I replace the player sprite?
docs.text: Replace Resources/Art/Characters/sovereign.png and keep the import settings (400 px/unit for characters). See Replacing art.

docs.title: Can I add my own weapons?
docs.text: Yes — add an ArmamentDef to ArmamentCatalog.All. See Adding content.

docs.title: Does changing a weapon id break saves?
docs.text: Yes. Saves store ids. Add entries freely; renaming or removing needs a migration.

docs.title: What frame rate should I expect?
docs.text: The game is 2D sprites in URP with a code-generated uGUI HUD. It runs comfortably at 60 fps on integrated graphics at 1280×720, which is the default window size.

docs.title: Why does the first frame hitch?
docs.text: HarvestGame builds the hub, camera, HUD and audio on start. The generated audio fallback clips are the most expensive part; shipping with the WAV files present avoids synthesis.

docs.title: Can I reduce the build size?
docs.text: Remove Resources/Audio if you will synthesise audio at runtime, and strip unused engine modules from Packages/manifest.json.

docs.title: Where do I report a bug?
docs.text: https://github.com/camenduru/ChosenOfTheHarvestDoc/issues — include your Unity version, platform, and the relevant log excerpt.

docs.title: Where is the changelog?
docs.text: Changelog.

docs.title: Is there a Discord?
docs.text: No. Use the issue tracker so answers stay searchable.

docs.title: AI disclosure
docs.text:
Artwork. The 49 sprites under Resources/Art were generated with a ComfyUI text-to-image workflow from prompts written for this project. They were then reviewed, background-removed, cropped, resized and colour-corrected. No third-party image was used as an input or style reference.

Audio. Not AI-generated. The 21 WAV clips are produced by the project's own synthesis code (Scripts/Core/AudioManager.cs).

Code, text, UI, design. Written for this project.

If you publish a game built on this template, describe the art honestly in your own store listing. Do not call these images "hand-drawn" or "painted".

docs.title: First, find the logs
docs.text: Log Location Editor Console window, or Editor.log in the Unity log folder Build BuildLogs/latest.log Smoke test BuildLogs/SMOKE_LOG.txt Player %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\ChosenOfTheHarvest\ChosenOfTheHarvest\Player.log macOS player ~/Library/Logs/ChosenOfTheHarvest/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Player.log Linux player ~/.config/unity3d/ChosenOfTheHarvest/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Player.log

docs.title: Scripts have compiler errors on first open
docs.text:
1. Confirm ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt says 6000.6.6f1.
  2. Open Window → Package Manager and check that Input System, uGUI and Universal RP are installed.
  3. Delete Library/ScriptAssemblies and Library/Bee, then re-open the project.

If the errors mention a missing UnityEngine.InputSystem, the Input System package did not resolve — see below.

docs.title: Package Manager cannot resolve a package
docs.text:
The project needs network access to packages.unity.com once. If you are offline:

  1. Open the project on a connected machine.
  2. Copy the resolved Library/PackageCache and Packages/packages-lock.json.
  3. Or vendor the packages into Packages/.

docs.title: Multiple Unity instances cannot open the same project
docs.text:
A previous batch-mode Unity process is still running and holding the lock. Close Unity, then end any lingering Unity.exe process:

Get-Process Unity -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force

docs.title: Text in the HUD is missing glyphs
docs.text:
HarvestHud uses Unity's built-in LegacyRuntime.ttf and falls back to an OS font. If a language needs glyphs the built-in font lacks, supply a font asset:

  1. Import a TTF/OTF.
  2. Assign it in HarvestHud.UiFont (replace the GetBuiltinResource call).
  3. Confirm it covers the glyphs in your en.json replacement.

docs.title: Pink / magenta everything
docs.text:
URP is not assigned. Set the pipeline asset:

  • Project Settings → Graphics → Default Render Pipeline → Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Settings/UniversalRP.asset
  • Project Settings → Quality → Render Pipeline Asset → the same file

docs.title: Sprites are huge or tiny
docs.text: ArtImporter sets characters to 400 px/unit and everything else to 100 px/unit. If you imported art outside that folder, set Pixels Per Unit manually to match.

docs.title: Sprites flicker or overlap incorrectly
docs.text: The template sorts sprites by world Z (Stage3D.SortOrder). Custom sprites with unusual pivots can fight for the same order. Adjust the pivot to bottom-centre or add a small bias.

docs.title: NullReferenceException in HarvestGame.Instance
docs.text: Something ran before the bootstrap. Code that touches HarvestGame.Instance must run after HarvestGame.Awake. If you add a system, start it from HarvestGame, not from Awake of an unrelated object.

docs.title: Ceremonies do nothing
docs.text: The altar has a cooldown. The toast The altar is resting (Ns) tells you how long is left. Also check grace, food and pearls meet the ceremony cost.

docs.title: A companion is stuck
docs.text: The follower uses NavGrid, which is rebuilt when the hub changes. If a companion is stuck after you place a building, pick the building up and put it back, or reload the save — both rebuild the nav grid.

docs.title: Building placement will not confirm
docs.text: Placement validates against RoomCollision and the hub bounds. Move the ghost until it turns valid; Esc cancels.

docs.title: Save fails
docs.text: HarvestSaveSystem writes to Application.persistentDataPath. A failure there usually means the disk is full or the OS blocked the folder. The log line [Save] slot=… path=… shows the exact path.

docs.title: Save loads but progress is wrong
docs.text:
Check the schema version:

[Load] slot=1 … version=4

If version is lower than HarvestSaveSystem.CurrentVersion, the repair pass in Migrate() ran — it fixes out-of-range values but cannot invent content that no longer exists (e.g. a removed weapon id).

docs.title: A corrupt save is not loading
docs.text: The loader falls back to <slot>.json.bak automatically and logs primary save corrupt; loaded .bak. If both fail, the file is unrecoverable; delete it to start a new slot.

docs.title: Linux build module is not installed
docs.text: Unity Hub → Installs → Add modules → Linux Build Support (Mono).

docs.title: The build succeeds but the smoke test fails
docs.text: Open BuildLogs/SMOKE_LOG.txt and search for Exception. The smoke test stops at the first unhandled exception, so the last SMOKE … line before the error tells you which system broke.

docs.title: Build log says another Unity instance is running
docs.text: Kill lingering Unity.exe processes (see above) and rebuild.

docs.title: The build is enormous
docs.text: Development builds include the Mono runtime and debug symbols. For a release build, enable Development Build = off, switch to IL2CPP, and enable code stripping.

docs.title: State survives between Play sessions
docs.text: A static field is missing its reset. Add it to the class's [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.SubsystemRegistration)] method. See Architecture.

docs.title: Only some systems reset
docs.text: Check that the class owns the field. HarvestState, Preferences, Bindings, Lexicon, SoundDirector, HarvestSaveSystem, Stage3D, HarvestHud, Creature, HexBolt, NavGrid and RoomCollision all have reset methods; anything new needs its own.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
If none of the above helps, open an issue with:

  • Unity version and OS;
  • target platform;
  • the exact error text and the surrounding log lines;
  • whether .\Tools\build.ps1 -RunSmoke passes.

https://github.com/camenduru/ChosenOfTheHarvestDoc/issues

docs.title: Bootstrap and game loop
docs.text:
HarvestGame is the template's single entry point. It builds the entire hub, owns the camera and HUD, creates the (disabled) expedition, and dispatches every player command. This page walks through its lifetime, the public surface it exposes to the rest of the codebase, and the interaction methods that other systems call.

File: Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Scripts/Core/GameBootstrap.cs, type ChosenOfTheHarvest.HarvestGame, Version = "1.0.0".

docs.title: Lifetime: Awake, no Start
docs.text:
HarvestGame has an Awake and an Update. There is deliberately no Start: one-time construction happens in Awake, in a fixed order, so that every later caller can assume the world exists.

void Awake()
{
    Instance = this;
    Preferences.Load();
    Bindings.Load();
    Application.targetFrameRate = 60;
    Application.runInBackground = true;
    Screen.SetResolution(1600, 900, FullScreenMode.Windowed);
    hubBounds = new Vector2(WorldWidth / 2f - 1f, WorldHeight / 2f - 1f);

    BuildCamera();
    BuildGlobalLight();

    Audio = SoundDirector.Create(transform);
    Audio.PlayMusic("music_hub");

    hubRoot = new GameObject("Hub");
    hubRoot.transform.SetParent(transform, false);

    BuildGround();
    BuildHarvestAltar();
    BuildPlayer();
    BuildResources();
    HarvestState.EnsureCompanionRecords();
    BuildCompanions();
    BuildPortal();
    BuildNpc();
    SpawnSavedSanctums();
    SpawnSavedMemorials();
    RebuildNavGrid();
    AssignBeds();
    RestorePenitents();

    var dungeonGo = new GameObject("Expedition");
    dungeonGo.transform.SetParent(transform, false);
    ExpeditionRef = dungeonGo.AddComponent<Expedition>();
    dungeonGo.SetActive(false);

    dayCycle = gameObject.AddComponent<SeasonCycle>();
    dayCycle.PhaseChanged += OnDayPhaseChanged;
    HarvestHudRef = HarvestHud.Create(dayCycle);
    Player.Died += OnPlayerDied;
    Preferences.Apply();

    bool smoke = System.Array.IndexOf(System.Environment.GetCommandLineArgs(), "-smoke") >= 0;
    if (smoke) gameObject.AddComponent<ProofTest>();
    else OpenTitleScreen();
}

flowchart TD
    A["Awake: Instance = this"] --> B["Preferences.Load + Bindings.Load"]
    B --> C["BuildCamera / BuildGlobalLight"]
    C --> D["SoundDirector.Create + music_hub"]
    D --> E["hubRoot + BuildGround"]
    E --> F["Altar · Player · 18 nodes"]
    F --> G["EnsureCompanionRecords + BuildCompanions"]
    G --> H["Portal · NPC · saved sanctums · memorials"]
    H --> I["NavGrid · AssignBeds · RestorePenitents"]
    I --> J["Expedition (inactive) + SeasonCycle + HUD"]
    J --> K["Player.Died += OnPlayerDied + Preferences.Apply"]
    K --> L{"-smoke on command line?"}
    L -->|yes| M["Add ProofTest"]
    L -->|no| N["OpenTitleScreen: paused, InputLocked"]

Two consequences of doing everything in Awake: the title screen opens with Time.timeScale = 0f and InputLocked = true, so hub simulation does not run while the menu is up; and loading a save later cannot re-run Awake, so ApplyLoadedSave destroys and respawns companions, sanctums and memorials instead.

Construction constants

The hub is 40 × 30 world units, with 10 trees and 8 rocks (WorldWidth, WorldHeight, TreeCount, RockCount). Ground tiles are duplicated from Art/World/ground until the plane is covered; there is no Terrain or Tilemap.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
The mode enum is private, because the rest of the code should ask questions rather than set the mode:

enum Mode { Hub, Expedition, Interior }
Transition Entry point What changes Hub → Expedition EnterExpedition(int act) hubRoot.SetActive(false), expedition activated, HarvestState.RollCurse(), health refilled, music_dungeon Expedition → Hub ExitExpedition(bool loot) ExpeditionRef.End(), hub reactivated, ClearRunState(), player returned to hubReturnPosition, autosave when loot Hub → Interior EnterInterior(Sanctum building) hubRoot.SetActive(false), interiorRoot built from the sanctum's record, camera distance 8.2 Interior → Hub ExitInterior() interiorRoot destroyed, player restored to interiorReturnPosition

The public read-only views of that private state are InExpedition, InInterior and IsPlacing; IsNight and IsDusk come from the SeasonCycle instead.

EnterExpedition() without an argument clamps currentAct to 0–2. A pilgrimage is gated: if (mode != Mode.Hub || ceremonyRunning) return;.

Mode is not a scene load

Hub, dungeon and interior all coexist as GameObjects under HarvestGame. Entering a dungeon disables hubRoot; it does not unload anything, so hub companions keep their state and their records.

docs.title: Input lock
docs.text:
public static bool InputLocked is a global gate, not a per-system flag. It is read by PlayerController.Update (movement, attack, dodge, rite, bomb), CompanionAgent, Sanctum.Update, and SeasonCycle.Update; when true the world freezes conceptually without changing Time.timeScale.

It is set by:

Action Sets Title screen, pause menu, any ShowMenu InputLocked = true (HarvestHud.ShowMenu) Resuming / HideMenu InputLocked = false Ceremony coroutine true for the duration Placement (BeginPlacement, BeginMove) true until confirm or cancel Photo mode true until ExitPhotoMode

Because it is static, a menu opened by any system blocks the player everywhere. That is the intent: one modal at a time.

docs.title: The frame: Update dispatch
docs.text:
The first three guards are worth memorising when you add a hotkey: rebinding and photo mode consume the frame entirely, and paused returns before the camera is updated (that is why the pause menu shows a frozen frame). After that the order is fixed:

  1. FollowCamera() and UpdateStatus().
  2. Interior mode: Interact() on the interact binding, then UpdatePrompt(), then return.
  3. Hub mode, unlocked: SagaSystem.Evaluate(this) at most once per second.
  4. Mute, then the placement branch (which consumes the frame), then InputLocked.
  5. Save, load, potion, Escape/pad-start pause.
  6. Q cycles the weapon, Z cycles the rite, E interacts, B builds, F opens the roster, I the inventory, K the catalog (hub only), C the map, J the quest log, R the nearest sanctum's management menu.
  7. UpdatePrompt() for the contextual hint.

docs.title: Camera, stage and HUD wiring
docs.text:
The camera is orthographic-free: a perspective camera at a fixed 45° pitch, looking along Stage3D.BillboardRotation, with sprites tilted to face it. There is no 2D pipeline camera trick beyond transparencySortMode = CustomAxis and transparencySortAxis = (0,0,1).

void BuildCamera()
{
    var go = new GameObject("Main Camera");
    go.tag = "MainCamera";
    go.AddComponent<AudioListener>();
    Cam = go.AddComponent<Camera>();
    Cam.orthographic = false;
    Cam.fieldOfView = Stage3D.CameraFov;
    Cam.nearClipPlane = 0.3f;
    Cam.farClipPlane = 100f;
    Cam.clearFlags = CameraClearFlags.SolidColor;
    Cam.backgroundColor = new Color(0.98f, 0.96f, 0.86f);
    Cam.transparencySortMode = TransparencySortMode.CustomAxis;
    Cam.transparencySortAxis = new Vector3(0f, 0f, 1f);
    cameraBase = Stage3D.P(0f, -3f) + CameraOffset;
    Cam.transform.position = cameraBase;
    Cam.transform.rotation = Stage3D.BillboardRotation;
}

Camera follow is FollowCamera, called from Update before dispatch. It clamps the target to the current mode's bounds (hub 14 × 11, interior 2.2 × 1.6, dungeon Player.Bounds), eases distance, and applies screen shake. The sky colour is owned by SeasonCycle (Apply() writes Cam.backgroundColor), so a phase change repaints the background without touching the bootstrap.

HarvestHud.Create(dayCycle) builds the whole UI and returns the component; the bootstrap keeps it as HarvestHudRef and calls SetPrompt, Toast, ShowMenu, HideMenu, SetVisible, SetGameplayVisible, SetUiScale, SetFpsVisible, SetHighContrast, ShowWarden, HideWarden, SetMinimap and FlashFade.

The light is one global Light2D (BuildGlobalLight), intensity 1, white. The URP 2D renderer is otherwise untouched at runtime.

docs.title: Building the hub
docs.text:
BuildGround tiles the ground sprite; BuildHarvestAltar places the statue and the altar and adds HarvestAltar; BuildPlayer attaches a billboard, a PoseAnimator and PlayerController, then sets Player.Bounds = hubBounds.

BuildResources spawns 10 trees and 8 rocks through SpawnNode, each with a GatherNode, a shadow, and a randomised position that keeps clear of the altar, the spawn point and the portal.

SpawnCompanion(index) is the only companion factory. It resolves the record, prefers Art/Characters/<lowercase name> then falls back to Art/Characters/companion, builds the billboard, adds CompanionAgent, calls BindRecord, and creates a CompanionNameTag.

public void SpawnCompanion(int index)
{
    HarvestState.EnsureCompanionRecords();
    var record = HarvestState.CompanionAt(index);
    if (record == null) return;

    var sprite = Resources.Load<Sprite>("Art/Characters/" + record.name.ToLowerInvariant());
    bool namedPortrait = sprite != null || record.name == "Amara";
    if (sprite == null) sprite = Resources.Load<Sprite>("Art/Characters/companion");
    // ... billboard, PoseAnimator, shadow, CompanionAgent, BindRecord, name tag
    companions.Add(agent);
}

docs.title: Saving from the loop
docs.text: SaveGame is private; it is reached with F5, the pause menu, or the slot menu. It flushes hauls, copies dirt and condition from live sanctums into their records, re-points each record, then calls HarvestSaveSystem.Save(). LoadGame() loads the active slot, repairs records, and calls ApplyLoadedSave, which respawns sanctums, companions and memorials in place. Autosave only happens on a victorious return from a pilgrimage (HarvestSaveSystem.Autosave()), and it respects Preferences.Autosave.

docs.title: Photo mode
docs.text: EnterPhotoMode pauses time, hides the HUD and every CompanionNameTag, and detaches the camera. PhotoUpdate moves the target with WASD/arrows, zooms with the wheel (4–16 units), and on F12 captures the backbuffer to persistentDataPath/Photos/photo_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss.png. Esc returns to the pause menu, not to play.

docs.title: The -smoke hook
docs.text:
Launching a player or the Editor play mode with -smoke on the command line adds ProofTest instead of opening the title screen:

bool smoke = System.Array.IndexOf(System.Environment.GetCommandLineArgs(), "-smoke") >= 0;
if (smoke) gameObject.AddComponent<ProofTest>();
else OpenTitleScreen();

ProofTest redirects saves to a scratch root (HarvestSaveSystem.UseTestRoot("ProofTest")), drives audio, four producing buildings, a pilgrimage, a curse, an omen, the kitchen discount, save/load and the menu, then writes state.txt next to persistentDataPath for screenshot tooling. It is inert without the flag: its Start disables the component.

Do not ship the smoke path

-smoke writes files and mutates a test save root. Keep it out of store builds by not launching with that argument; no build script strips it.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text: Chosen of the Harvest is a runtime-assembled Unity template: one scene, one MonoBehaviour, and no prefabs. Everything the player sees — camera, ground, buildings, companions, HUD, dungeon — is created from code when the game starts. This page explains the layers that make that possible, how a frame travels through them, and which rules keep the codebase reskinnable.

docs.title: One scene, zero prefabs
docs.text:
The only authored scene is Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Scenes/ChosenOfTheHarvest.unity. It contains a single GameObject named Game with one component, HarvestGame. There are no prefab assets, no [SerializeField] graph, and no scene references to repair:

// Editor/BuildGame.cs — the scene is generated, not hand-authored.
var scene = EditorSceneManager.NewScene(NewSceneSetup.EmptyScene, NewSceneMode.Single);
var game = new GameObject("Game");
game.AddComponent<HarvestGame>();
EditorSceneManager.SaveScene(scene, ScenePath);

Every object that lives in the world is built by HarvestGame.Awake through helpers in Stage3D (CreateBillboard, CreateFlat, CreateShadow) and every piece of UI is built by HarvestHud.Create, which constructs the Canvas, its CanvasScaler, all Text labels and the menu panel in code.

Why this matters for a template

A buyer can rename the project, drop in new sprites and audio, and press Play. Nothing breaks because a prefab GUID moved, because there are no prefabs to move. The cost is that the bootstrap file is large.

All gameplay types live in the namespace ChosenOfTheHarvest, with no assembly definition, so everything compiles into Assembly-CSharp and can reference everything else without using directives. The Editor scripts are the only exception: ChosenOfTheHarvest.EditorTools.

Namespace names are the API

Because there are no nested namespaces, a type name is globally unique inside the project. Companion is CompanionAgent, Dungeon is Expedition, Building is Sanctum, Enemy is Creature, Spell is Rite. The file names and the type names intentionally differ; use the type names in code.

docs.title: How a frame flows
docs.text:
HarvestGame.Update never simulates anything itself. It reads input, decides which mode is active, and forwards to a method that opens a menu, starts a coroutine, or mutates state. Movement and attacks live in PlayerController.Update and are gated by the same flags.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Input as Keyboard / Gamepad
    participant Boot as HarvestGame.Update
    participant Mode as Mode dispatch
    participant Sys as Systems
    participant State as HarvestState
    participant HUD as HarvestHud

    Input->>Boot: poll Bindings / raw keys
    alt rebinding or photo mode
        Boot->>Boot: HandleRebind / PhotoUpdate, return
    else paused
        Boot->>Boot: return
    end
    Boot->>HUD: FollowCamera + UpdateStatus
    Boot->>Mode: Interior / Hub / Expedition
    Mode->>Sys: Interact, Build, ceremony, roster
    Sys->>State: mutate HarvestState.Data
    State-->>HUD: NotifyChanged (clamp) then poll
    HUD->>HUD: Refresh reads Data + StatusLine

The actual branches, in order, are visible in the source:

void Update()
{
    var kb = Keyboard.current;
    if (kb == null) return;

    if (rebinding != null) { HandleRebind(kb); return; }
    if (photoMode) { PhotoUpdate(kb); return; }
    if (paused) return;

    FollowCamera();
    UpdateStatus();

    if (mode == Mode.Interior)
    {
        if (Bindings.Pressed(Bindings.Action.Interact)) Interact();
        UpdatePrompt();
        return;
    }

    if (mode == Mode.Hub && !InputLocked)
    {
        questTimer -= Time.deltaTime;
        if (questTimer <= 0f) { questTimer = 1f; SagaSystem.Evaluate(this); }
    }

    if (Bindings.Pressed(Bindings.Action.Mute)) ToggleMute();
    if (placementGhost != null) { HandlePlacementInput(kb); return; }
    if (InputLocked) { HarvestHudRef.SetPrompt(""); return; }
    // ... save, load, potion, pause, weapon/rite cycling, interact, build, menus
}

Two details are easy to get wrong:

  • Unity does not order Update calls between components. HarvestGame.Update and PlayerController.Update both run in the same phase; the only contract is that HarvestGame.InputLocked is checked by the player, companions and buildings before they act.
  • The HUD pulls, it does not subscribe. HarvestState.Changed exists and is invoked by NotifyChanged, but no shipped script subscribes. HarvestHud.Update calls Refresh() every frame and reads HarvestState.Data plus HarvestGame.Instance.StatusLine.

docs.title: Dependency rules
docs.text:
1. World objects never open menus. They call HarvestGame.Instance for FloatingText, Toast, Shake, HitFeedback and mode queries, and return.
  2. Nothing writes HarvestState.Data without NotifyChanged(). That call is where resource caps are enforced, so a producer that skips it can exceed the cap until the next write.
  3. Catalogs are static read-only tables. They never reference HarvestGame except through HarvestState.Data for the equipped id (ArmamentCatalog.Current).
  4. Save/load is a boundary, not a system. HarvestSaveSystem serialises HarvestState.Data and nothing else; runtime objects are rebuilt from it.
  5. Presentation reads state and never owns it. Stage3D has no game rules; HarvestHud holds no resource counts.

docs.title: Why this suits a reskin
docs.text:
• Art is addressed by path, not by reference. Resources.Load<Sprite>("Art/Sanctums/" + type) means a new farm.png replaces the farm with no code change; ArtImporter forces the sprite import settings for anything under Resources/Art/.
  • Numbers live in one file per family. Damage in WeaponCatalog.cs, rites in SpellCatalog.cs, relics in RelicCatalog.cs, attire in GearCatalog.cs, costs in Building.cs. Rebalancing never touches the bootstrap.
  • Copy is localised through one facade. Lexicon.Get(key, fallback) with English and a pseudo-locale in Resources/Localization; hard-coded fallbacks keep the game readable if a table is missing.
  • The HUD is generated from layout code. Changing the accent colour or the reference resolution is a local edit in Hud.cs, not a canvas rebuild.

docs.title: Trade-offs
docs.text:
Know what you are inheriting

  • GameBootstrap.cs is ~4.2k lines and owns menus, ceremonies, building and photo mode. It is the file you will edit most, and the one most likely to conflict when merging.
  • Static mutable state (HarvestState.Data, HarvestGame.InputLocked, NavGrid, RoomCollision) makes the systems easy to call but hard to unit-test in isolation; the shipped ProofTest drives the real game loop instead of mocking it.
  • Nothing is data-driven through ScriptableObject, so designers edit C# tables rather than assets in the Inspector.
  • Resources loading is simple but loads everything under those folders into the build; a shipping project with a large art budget should move to Addressables.

docs.title: Static state and Fast Enter Playmode
docs.text:
Unity 6.6 and newer let you enter Play mode without a domain reload, which keeps static fields alive between sessions. The Asset Store requires packages to work in that mode (submission guideline 2.5.h).

The template therefore resets every mutable static in a [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.SubsystemRegistration)] method owned by the class that declares the field:

Class What it resets HarvestGame Instance, InputLocked HarvestState Data, CurrentCurse, RunHealthPenalty, Changed Preferences loaded flag and every option to its default Bindings loaded so bindings reload from PlayerPrefs Lexicon loaded, locale, cached values SoundDirector Instance HarvestSaveSystem rootOverride Stage3D cached material and sprites HarvestHud cached font and white sprite Creature the All registry HexBolt the projectile pool NavGrid grid buffers RoomCollision obstacle list and bounds 
[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.SubsystemRegistration)]
static void ResetStatics()
{
    Instance = null;
    InputLocked = false;
}

If you add a static field

Add it to the owning class's reset method. A static that survives a Play session is the most common Fast-Enter-Playmode bug.

docs.title: State and save data
docs.text: All durable progression lives in one serialisable object, HarvestSaveData, and every system reaches it through the static facade HarvestState. HarvestSaveSystem turns that object into JSON slots with atomic writes, a backup copy and a schema version. This page documents the fields, the derived values computed from them, and the exact save-on-disk contract.

    Save -->|"HarvestState.Data = loaded"| State

Nothing else is persisted. Placed buildings exist twice — as live Sanctum components and as SanctumData records — and the bootstrap syncs them before saving. Companion agents likewise point at CompanionRecord instances rather than owning their own numbers.

public static class HarvestState
{
    public static HarvestSaveData Data = new HarvestSaveData();

    /// <summary>Runtime-only pilgrimage state; never serialized.</summary>
    public static Curse CurrentCurse;
    public static int RunHealthPenalty;

    public static event Action Changed;
    // ...
}
Member Type Description Data HarvestSaveData The live save object; replaced wholesale by load and reset CurrentCurse Curse Runtime-only modifier for the current pilgrimage RunHealthPenalty int Runtime-only max-health penalty (25 for Frailty) Changed event Action Raised at the end of NotifyChanged Reset() void Replaces Data with a fresh object and notifies

Reset() is what "New game" calls, so it also resets day, resources, creed and all records. It does not delete save files; that is HarvestSaveSystem.Delete.

Static data survives scene loads

HarvestState.Data is a static field, so it outlives the scene. The template never loads a second scene, but a host project that does must call Reset() or explicitly reload a slot.

docs.title: NotifyChanged and the event
docs.text:
public static void NotifyChanged()
{
    if (Data != null)
    {
        Data.wood = Mathf.Clamp(Data.wood, 0, WoodCap);
        Data.stone = Mathf.Clamp(Data.stone, 0, StoneCap);
        Data.food = Mathf.Clamp(Data.food, 0, FoodCap);
        Data.herbs = Mathf.Clamp(Data.herbs, 0, HerbCap);
        Data.meals = Mathf.Clamp(Data.meals, 0, MealCap);
        Data.medicine = Mathf.Clamp(Data.medicine, 0, MedicineCap);
        Data.potions = Mathf.Clamp(Data.potions, 0, PotionCap);
        Data.bombs = Mathf.Clamp(Data.bombs, 0, BombCap);
    }

    Changed?.Invoke();
}

Changed is invoked on every notify: 46 call sites in GameBootstrap, 8 in Building, 8 in Dungeon, and one each in GatherNode, Creature, CompanionAgent, PlayerController, SeasonCycle, SagaSystem, GameState and HarvestSaveSystem.

The shipped HUD polls instead of listening

No script in the template subscribes to HarvestState.Changed. HarvestHud.Update calls Refresh() every frame and re-reads HarvestState.Data and HarvestGame.Instance.StatusLine. The event is therefore free to subscribe to from your own code, but do not expect it to be the reason the HUD updates.

docs.title: Save files and slots
docs.text:
Slot Constant Path Autosave AutosaveSlot = 0 <persistentDataPath>/save_auto.json Manual 1 FirstSlot = 1 <persistentDataPath>/save_slot_1.json Manual 2 FirstSlot + 1 <persistentDataPath>/save_slot_2.json Manual 3 SlotCount = 3 <persistentDataPath>/save_slot_3.json Legacy — <persistentDataPath>/save.json (read-only fallback for slot 1)

ActiveSlot is persisted in PlayerPrefs under choth_active_save_slot and clamped to 0–3. Manual saves update it; autosaves do not, so pressing F5 after an autosave still targets the player's chosen slot.

UseTestRoot("name") repoints writes to a subdirectory and deletes its files; this is what ProofTest uses. UseDefaultRoot() restores persistentDataPath.

docs.title: Writing a save
docs.text:
Save(slot) is atomic enough to survive a crash mid-write:

HarvestState.Data.saveVersion = CurrentVersion;
HarvestState.EnsureCompanionRecords();

string path = SlotPath(slot);
string temp = path + ".tmp";
string backup = path + ".bak";
string json = JsonUtility.ToJson(HarvestState.Data, true);

Directory.CreateDirectory(Root);
File.WriteAllText(temp, json);
if (File.Exists(path)) File.Copy(path, backup, true);   // previous good save
File.Copy(temp, path, true);
File.Delete(temp);

JsonUtility is used with prettyPrint = true, so a save is human-readable and diffable. The type is plain [Serializable] classes with public fields; there are no custom converters, so renaming a field drops its data.

docs.title: Loading, recovery and migration
docs.text:
Load(slot) clamps the slot, falls back to the legacy save.json for slot 1, then tries the primary file. If parsing fails it retries the .bak:

if (!TryRead(path, out var loaded))
{
    string backup = path + ".bak";
    if (!File.Exists(backup) || !TryRead(backup, out loaded))
    {
        Debug.LogError("[Load] Both save and backup failed: " + path);
        return false;
    }
    Debug.LogWarning("[Load] primary save corrupt; loaded .bak");
}

HarvestState.Data = loaded;
Migrate();
if (slot != AutosaveSlot) ActiveSlot = slot;
HarvestState.NotifyChanged();

Migrate() runs only when saveVersion < 4, and then repairs unconditionally:

  1. Every building gets level ≥ 1, condition = 100 if non-positive, and a non-null interior list.
  2. EnsureLoadout() repairs attire/armour/charm/rite ids.
  3. Every companion record gets inReflection ≥ -1 and priority clamped 0–2.
  4. saveVersion = CurrentVersion.
  5. EnsureCompanionRecords() then reconciles the record list with Data.companions, creates missing records, clamps needs, levels and ages, and de-duplicates names.

EnsureCompanionRecords also performs the socialVersion migrations: version 1 clears friend/partner, version 2 clears parentA/parentB/childDay. This is separate from the file schema, because relationship fields were added after the save format shipped.

Slot summaries do not load the slot

SlotSummary(slot) reads the JSON only to format "MM-dd HH:mm | Day N | Act N", where the act is Clamp(campaignStage + 1, 1, 3). It returns "empty" if the file is missing.

docs.title: Autosave
docs.text:
public static void Autosave()
{
    if (!Preferences.Autosave) return;
    Save(AutosaveSlot);
}

There is exactly one autosave trigger in the shipped game: returning from a pilgrimage with loot == true (ExitExpedition). It is off by default only if the player turns it off in Preferences; Preferences.Autosave defaults to true.

docs.title: Update order inside one frame
docs.text:
Update order between components is not guaranteed by Unity, so the template makes every system self-gating on HarvestGame.InputLocked rather than relying on ordering.

sequenceDiagram
    participant G as HarvestGame
    participant P as PlayerController
    participant H as HarvestHud
    participant C as CompanionAgent
    participant S as Sanctum
    participant D as SeasonCycle

    par Unity Update phase (unordered)
        G->>G: camera, status, mode dispatch
        P->>P: movement, attack, dodge if !InputLocked
        C->>C: needs, jobs, pathing if !InputLocked
        S->>S: production timer if !InputLocked
        D->>D: phase timer if !InputLocked
    end
    H->>H: Refresh reads state + StatusLine

docs.title: How to add a new system
docs.text:
1. Pick the layer. If it owns persistent numbers, it belongs beside HarvestState. If it is a live object, it belongs in Scripts/World, Scripts/Dungeon or Scripts/Followers. If it is a table, it belongs in Scripts/Combat next to the other catalogs.
  2. Add state, not statics. Put new persistent fields on HarvestSaveData, give them an initializer, and mutate through HarvestState.Data. New fields are picked up automatically by JsonUtility; absent fields keep their initializer on old saves.
  3. Gate on InputLocked. Anything with an Update must return early when the flag is set, exactly like Sanctum and CompanionAgent.
  4. Notify once. Batch the mutations, call HarvestState.NotifyChanged() at the end so caps apply and listeners fire.
  5. Spawn from the bootstrap. Add a Build…/Spawn… method to HarvestGame and call it from Awake in dependency order; keep a list if the system needs to be saved or rebuilt.
  6. Expose text through Lexicon. Use Lexicon.Get("your.key", "Fallback") and add the key to both Resources/Localization/en.json and xx.json.
  7. Hook one hotkey. Add the key to Update, or add an action to Bindings.Action and a default in the Defaults array.

A minimal, correctly-wired component looks like this:

public class TitheChest : MonoBehaviour
{
    float timer;

    void Update()
    {
        if (HarvestGame.InputLocked) return;   // respect menus, ceremonies, placement

        timer += Time.deltaTime;
        if (timer < 20f) return;
        timer -= 20f;

        HarvestState.Data.grace += 1;          // mutate state
        HarvestState.NotifyChanged();          // clamp caps + raise Changed
        HarvestGame.Instance.FloatingText(
            Stage3D.Above(transform.position, 1.5f), "+1 grace", Color.white);
    }
}

If you add a save field that needs repair

HarvestSaveSystem.Migrate() only runs when the file's saveVersion is lower than CurrentVersion. Adding a field does not require a version bump; changing the meaning of an existing field does. In that case raise CurrentVersion and extend Migrate() so old slots are repaired rather than silently misread.

docs.text: Every system follows the same shape: a definition class, a static readonly array, and lookup helpers. Adding content means adding an entry to that array.

docs.title: Add a weapon
docs.text:
Scripts/Combat/WeaponCatalog.cs:

public static readonly ArmamentDef FanScythe = new ArmamentDef
{
    Type = ArmamentType.Scythe,
    Id = "fanscythe",
    Name = "Fan Scythe",
    BaseDamage = 32,
    Cooldown = 0.46f,
    Range = 2.4f,
    ArcDot = -0.2f,
    Knockback = 3f,
    ComboCount = 3,
    ComboWindow = 0.5f,
    Lunge = 0.24f,
    BleedDps = 4f,
    BleedDuration = 3f,
    Tint = new Color(0.9f, 0.8f, 1f)
};

Then register it:

public static readonly ArmamentDef[] All =
{
    Sword, Axe, Dagger, Spear, Hammer, Gauntlets, Scythe, Mace,
    Flail, Rapier, Cleaver, Halberd, FanScythe
};

Then implement the effect in GameState.cs, e.g. inside GraceMultiplier:

public static float GraceMultiplier =>
    (Data.creedGrace == "feast" ? 1.5f : 1f) *
    (HasOmen("moon") ? 1.15f : 1f) *
    (HasOmen("lantern") ? 1.1f : 1f) * ...

Warning

Omen ids are written into saves. Adding is safe; renaming is not.

docs.title: Add a sanctum type
docs.text:
Four edits, in order:

  1. Enum — Scripts/Buildings/Building.cs:
public enum SanctumType
{
    Farm, Shrine, Bed, Lumberyard, Quarry, Kitchen,
    Storage, HerbGarden, Apothecary, TeaHouse, Memorial, Reflection,
    SunBath, Obelisk, Temple, Sawmill, Stoneworks, WheatField,
    BellTower, Reliquary, Orchard
}

  1. Costs — add cases to CostWood, CostStone, and optionally UpgradeCostWood/UpgradeCostStone.

  2. Label and localisation — add a case to Sanctum.Label's switch and a building.orchard key to en.json. (The label falls back to the enum name, so this is cosmetic.)

  3. Sprite — add Resources/Art/Sanctums/orchard.png. The loader is:

string art = type.ToString().ToLowerInvariant();
var sprite = Resources.Load<Sprite>("Art/Sanctums/" + art);

The enum member and the file name must match

SpriteForSanctum derives the file name from the enum member. If you add Orchard and forget orchard.png, the building silently falls back to the shrine sprite.

Also add the build-menu entry where the game lists buildable types (GameBootstrap.ShowBuildMenu / BuildSummary) and a height case in TargetHeightForSanctum.

{
    Melee, Fast, Brute, Caster, Charger, Exploder,
    Shielder, Summoner, Healer, Archer, Slammer, Assassin, Howler

  2. add a behaviour branch in Creature.Update (the existing archetypes show the pattern: charger, summoner, healer, slammer, assassin);
  3. add the archetype to the spawn table in Dungeon.cs.

docs.text:
Scripts/Core/QuestSystem.cs:

static readonly string[] Keys =
{
    "quest.buildfarm", "quest.hymn", "quest.reflection",
    "quest.forest", "quest.temple", "quest.sanctum",
    "quest.companions", "quest.devotion", "quest.orchard", "quest.done"
};

Update FinalStage, add a case in the Evaluate switch with the completion condition, and add quest.orchard to en.json. Rewards are automatic: stages 0–4 pay 2 devotion, stages 5+ pay 4.

docs.title: Add a localisation key
docs.text:
Resources/Localization/en.json:

{
  "key": "hud.orchard",
  "value": "Orchard {0}/{1}"
}

Read it with Lexicon.Get("hud.orchard", "Orchard") or Lexicon.Format("hud.orchard", "Orchard {0}/{1}", a, b). Add the same key to xx.json if you want the pseudo-locale to cover it (any placeholder value is fine — it exists to test layout).

docs.title: Add a save field
docs.text:
1. Add the field to HarvestSaveData with a default:
public int orchardYield = 1;
  1. Bump the schema:
// Scripts/Core/SaveSystem.cs
public const int CurrentVersion = 5;
  1. Extend the repair pass in Migrate() so old saves get a sane value:
if (HarvestState.Data.orchardYield < 1)
    HarvestState.Data.orchardYield = 1;

Migrate() is an idempotent repair pass rather than a per-version chain: it runs after every load and fixes any field that is out of range. That keeps old saves loadable without writing one migration method per version.

docs.title: Replacing art
docs.text: Every visible sprite in the template is a loose PNG under Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Resources/Art, loaded by path at runtime. There are no atlases, sprite sheets, prefabs or material variants to keep in sync — replace a file, keep its name, and the game picks it up. The only contract is the import settings applied by ArtImporter, which this page documents in full.

docs.title: How sprites are loaded
docs.text:
GameBootstrap calls Resources.Load<Sprite>("Art/<folder>/<name>") and builds a camera-facing billboard with Stage3D. Six folders, 49 files:

Folder Files Loaded by Characters/ 12 player, companions, NPCs, every creature Sanctums/ 22 the 20 sanctum types, plus chest and door World/ 5 ground, altar, statue, tree, rock Expedition/ 5 floors, candle, projectile, skull Wardens/ 4 three boss bodies, plus unused stag_antlers UI/ 1 the omen card icon

The complete set, so you can diff your replacements against it:

Characters   companion husk iris liora merchant mira nadia oracle
             sable sovereign yafit yara
Sanctums     apothecary bed belltower chest door farm herbgarden kitchen
             lumberyard memorial obelisk quarry reflection reliquary sawmill
             shrine stoneworks storage sunbath teahouse temple wheatfield
World        altar ground rock statue tree
Expedition   candle floor_reflection floor_stones projectile skull
Wardens      mire_body stag_antlers stag_body sultan_body
UI           omen

One creature sprite, twelve archetypes

All twelve Creature.Archetype variants share Characters/husk.png and are distinguished by a per-archetype tint applied in Dungeon.SpawnCreature. To give an archetype its own art you must add a load call, not a file — see Adding content.

docs.title: The import contract
docs.text:
Editor/ArtImporter.cs is an AssetPostprocessor. It only touches textures whose path contains /Resources/Art/, and it forces the following on every one of them:

Setting Value Why it matters Texture type Sprite a Texture2D reference will not resolve Sprite mode Single no sheets, no sub-sprites Pixels per unit 400 under /Characters/, else 100 sets the sprite's world size Filter mode Bilinear smooth scaling, no pixel-art crunch Mip maps off billboards are always near the camera Alpha is transparency on required for the cut-out edges Compression CompressedHQ keeps gradients clean Mesh type FullRect tiled ground and scaled props need the full quad Fallback physics shape off nothing uses sprite colliders

Because the mesh is FullRect, sprite.bounds is the whole rectangle, transparent pixels included. That has two direct consequences:

  1. Keep the character's feet on the bottom edge of the canvas, or it will hover.
  2. Do not add padding to make the canvas a convenient size — the padding counts.

docs.title: Step 1 — Replace the file, keep the name
docs.text:
1. Create your PNG at the exact path of the file you are replacing.
  2. Keep the file name lowercase; the code builds it from an enum or a record name.
  3. Delete the old PNG rather than adding farm2.png next to it — nothing loads farm2.
  4. If the sprite is new (not a replacement), also wire it up; see Adding content.
# What is actually on disk, with pixel sizes
find Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Resources/Art -name '*.png' \
  -exec file {} \; | sort

# Same check on Windows
Get-ChildItem Assets\ChosenOfTheHarvest\Resources\Art -Recurse -Filter *.png |
  ForEach-Object {
    $img = [System.Drawing.Image]::FromFile($_.FullName)
    "{0}x{1}`t{2}" -f $img.Width, $img.Height, $_.FullName
    $img.Dispose()
  }

docs.title: Step 2 — Match the framing
docs.text:
The template's art was authored to one rhythm. Following it means no code changes.

Slot Shipped size World result Characters 1024 px tall, 338–665 wide 2.56 units at 400 PPU; player is scaled to 0.75, followers to 0.6 Sanctums 768 px tall, 235–1248 wide fitted to 1.6–2.8 units tall, clamped to 3 units wide World props 512–768 px fitted to targetHeight (tree 3.2, rock 1.8, altar 2.6, statue 2.4) Ground 512 × 512 5.12 units at 100 PPU, tiled across the 40 × 30 hub Omen icon 343 × 512 drawn in menus at text height Wardens 1024 px tall fitted to 2.5–2.6 units, clamped to 2.8 units wide

Characters are not fitted to a target height — the root scale is fixed, so PPU is the only lever on their size. A 1024 px portrait at 400 PPU is 2.56 units; if you export at 512 px and keep 400 PPU, the character is half height.

Buildings and props are fitted, so a different resolution is safe as long as the aspect ratio is right. Stage3D.CreateBillboard uses min(targetHeight / height, maxWidth / width), so a wide building is limited by width and ends up shorter than its neighbours.

docs.title: Step 3 — Force the reimport
docs.text:
Saving over a PNG usually triggers a reimport. When it does not (Unity still has the old texture in memory), force it:

// Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Editor/ReimportArt.cs
using UnityEditor;
using UnityEngine;

public static class ReimportArt
{
    [MenuItem("Chosen of the Harvest/Reimport art")]
    public static void Run()
    {
        var guids = AssetDatabase.FindAssets(
            "t:Texture2D", new[] { "Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Resources/Art" });

        foreach (var guid in guids)
        {
            string path = AssetDatabase.GUIDToAssetPath(guid);
            AssetDatabase.ImportAsset(path, ImportAssetOptions.ForceUpdate);
        }

        AssetDatabase.Refresh();
    }
}

The menu item lives under the template's existing top-level menu, next to the two build entries in BuildGame.cs.

docs.title: Step 4 — Verify in play mode
docs.text:
1. Enter Play and look at the hub: player, followers, trees, rocks, altar, portal.
  2. Press B and page through the build menu — every sanctum shows its icon.
  3. Enter an expedition (E at the portal) and check floors, walls, doors, candles.
  4. Reach a Warden and confirm the body sprite and its height.
  5. Open the pause menu (Esc) and inspect the omen card icon in the deck.

Silent fallbacks hide mistakes

SpriteForSanctum falls back to Sanctums/shrine and unknown companions fall back to Characters/companion. A typo therefore looks like the wrong sprite, never like an error. If a building suddenly looks like a shrine, check the file name before anything else.

docs.title: Naming traps
docs.text:
Enum → file name. The sanctum path is the lowercased enum member:

string art = type.ToString().ToLowerInvariant();
var sprite = Resources.Load<Sprite>("Art/Sanctums/" + art);
if (sprite == null) sprite = Resources.Load<Sprite>("Art/Sanctums/shrine");

So TeaHouse → teahouse.png, WheatField → wheatfield.png, BellTower → belltower.png. Rename the enum to TeaRoom and the code looks for tearoom.png; miss that and every tea house becomes a shrine.

Record name → file name. Companions load "Art/Characters/" + record.name.ToLowerInvariant(). Names come from CompanionCatalog.Names; to give a companion a portrait, add characters/<name>.png in lowercase. Amara deliberately has no file and uses the shared companion.png, so a missing portrait is not an error.

Case on other platforms. Windows resolves Resources.Load paths case-insensitively; Linux and console builds do not. Always ship lowercase names even if your local test passes with Farm.png.

Warden parts. WardenAppearance.Init loads only stag_body, mire_body and sultan_body. stag_antlers.png ships with the template but is not referenced — the Stag's antlers are part of its body sprite. Replacing the antlers file changes nothing.

docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Building shows a shrine file name does not match the lowercased enum member Character floats or sinks transparent padding above/below the feet in a FullRect sprite Character too small or huge PPU was not forced to 400 — the importer did not run Sprite is invisible texture imported as Default, not Sprite Ground shows seams tile is not square, or PPU is not 100 Building looks squashed aspect ratio changed while height fitting stayed on Double shadow a shadow is baked into the PNG; the code adds its own Blurry at distance mipmaps were enabled by a platform override

docs.title: Replacing audio
docs.text: Audio is plain AudioSource and AudioClip — no mixer, no middleware, no ScriptableObject bank. SoundDirector owns two 2D sources and loads clips from Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Resources/Audio/<key>.wav, where <key> is one of 21 fixed names. Anything missing falls back to a synthesized tone, so the game never goes silent while you work.

docs.title: The 21 keys
docs.text:
SoundBank.UsedKeys is the single source of truth. Files are loaded by exactly these names, without the extension.

Key Kind Fires from music_hub loop hub entry, returning from an expedition music_dungeon loop every non-Warden expedition room music_boss0 loop Act I Warden room music_boss1 loop Act II Warden room music_boss2 loop Act III Warden room swing one-shot melee attacks, bomb throw hit one-shot damage to a creature, projectile impact hurt one-shot damage to the player die one-shot any death, including a Warden gather one-shot harvesting a tree or rock build one-shot placing or upgrading a sanctum, interior pieces pickup one-shot collecting production, potions, chest loot chest one-shot opening a reward chest ceremony one-shot hymns, rites, repairs, omens, quest completion feast one-shot feast and plenty ceremonies sacrifice one-shot sacrifice ceremony, bomb detonation portal one-shot entering or leaving an expedition, Warden teleports sharpen one-shot sharpening at the forge ui one-shot opening or choosing a menu entry error one-shot refused actions and unaffordable builds slam one-shot heavy Warden attacks 
# Every key that currently has a file

  xargs -n1 basename | sed 's/\.wav$//' | sort

Placeholder art is deliberate

The shipped WAVs are original synthesized tones, not extracted audio. They are safe to ship while prototyping and safe to delete when you replace them — the code regenerates an equivalent tone for any key whose file is absent.

docs.title: Step 1 — Replace the clip
docs.text:
1. Export your clip as <key>.wav using one of the 21 names above.
  2. Drop it into Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Resources/Audio/, overwriting the old file.
  3. Do not rename the file to a friendly title; the key is the lookup path.
  4. For a brand-new sound, add the key to SoundBank.UsedKeys first (see below).
Resources/Audio/
  music_hub.wav        music_dungeon.wav
  music_boss0.wav      music_boss1.wav      music_boss2.wav
  swing.wav  hit.wav   hurt.wav   die.wav
  gather.wav build.wav pickup.wav chest.wav
  ceremony.wav feast.wav sacrifice.wav portal.wav
  sharpen.wav ui.wav   error.wav  slam.wav

docs.title: Step 2 — Match the format
docs.text:
The generated clips are mono at 22 050 Hz. Your files do not have to match, because nothing resamples at runtime, but the shipped import settings are a useful baseline:

Import setting Shipped value Effect Load type DecompressOnLoad decoded up front, no first-play hitch Compression Vorbis, quality 1 small build, fine for short SFX Preload audio data off saves a little memory at startup Force to mono off stereo is preserved Normalize on consistent perceived loudness 3D on in the meta, ignored at runtime both sources use spatialBlend = 0

Music clips are 24 s (music_hub, music_dungeon) and 16 s (the three Warden themes). The synthesized versions fade the first and last 0.12 s so the loop point is clickless; if you author a replacement, match its ends or accept a seam. The loop itself is forced at runtime (musicSource.loop = true), so the importer's loop flag does nothing.

One source means shared pitch

SFX play through a single AudioSource with PlayOneShot. Volume per call is respected, but pitch is a property of the source: setting a pitch for a new sound also retunes every one-shot still playing. Values are clamped to 0.55 – 1.9, so extreme pitch tricks are not available without a second source.

docs.title: Step 3 — Verify what actually loaded
docs.text:
SoundDirector tracks four counters: ClipCount, PlaceholderClipCount, UsedClipCount and MissingPlaceholderCount. The smoke test prints them:

audio=True clips=21 placeholderAudio=21 usedAudio=21 missingAudio=0 archive=21

A quick manual check from the console or a test hook:

var audio = HarvestGame.Instance.Audio;
Debug.Log($"clips={audio.ClipCount} used={audio.UsedClipCount} " +
          $"missing={audio.MissingPlaceholderCount} music={audio.CurrentMusic}");

clips counts everything in the dictionary, including synthesized fallbacks; placeholderAudio counts only files found in Resources/Audio. If placeholderAudio is lower than 21, a file name does not match its key.

docs.title: Step 4 — Tune the mix
docs.text:
There is no mixer asset. Volume is arithmetic in SoundDirector.ApplyVolumes():

Stage Default Where Master 0.85 Preferences.MasterVolume Music 0.65 Preferences.MusicVolume SFX 0.85 Preferences.SfxVolume Music source 0.34 × master × music SoundDirector SFX source 0.75 × master × sfx SoundDirector

At the defaults that is roughly 0.19 for music and 0.54 for SFX. Per-call volume multiplies on top and is clamped to 0 – 1.

// Change the balance for every source, then re-apply.
Preferences.SetMaster(0.8f);
Preferences.SetMusic(0.5f);
Preferences.SetSfx(0.9f);
Preferences.Apply();          // pushes the values into SoundDirector

Mute is separate from volume: M toggles AudioSource.mute on both sources and persists to PlayerPrefs under choth_audio_muted. Music keeps playing silently while muted, so unmuting resumes mid-track rather than restarting it.

docs.title: Adding a new sound
docs.text:
1. Add the key to UsedKeys (and a description to Palette, which documents the intended timbre and is otherwise unused).
  2. Drop <key>.wav into Resources/Audio/.
  3. Call SoundDirector.Sfx("<key>", volume, pitch) or HarvestGame.Instance.Audio.Play("<key>", volume, pitch).
// AudioArchive.cs
public static readonly string[] UsedKeys =
{
    "music_hub", "music_dungeon", "music_boss0", "music_boss1", "music_boss2",
    "swing", "hit", "hurt", "die", "gather", "build", "pickup", "chest",
    "ceremony", "feast", "sacrifice", "portal", "sharpen", "ui", "error",
    "slam", "forge"
};

public static readonly string[] Palette =
{
    // ... one entry per key, in the same order ...
    "heavy stone impact", "anvil ring"
};

// Anywhere with a UnityEngine reference
SoundDirector.Sfx("forge", 0.75f, 1.1f);
HarvestGame.Instance.Audio.Play("forge", 0.6f, 0.9f);

Resources/Audio/forge.wav

A key without a file is silent, not synthesized

The synthesized fallback exists only for the 21 built-in keys, because BuildClips() allocates them by name. A key added to UsedKeys with no matching WAV is counted in MissingPlaceholderCount and produces no sound at all. Ship the file with the key.

Music can be switched the same way. PlayMusic is a no-op if the requested key is already playing, so it is safe to call every time a room loads:

SoundDirector.Instance?.PlayMusic("music_dungeon");

docs.text: Every number that matters is a constant or a catalog entry in C#. This page maps the tuning surface so you know which file to open.

docs.title: Difficulty
docs.text:
Difficulty is a three-step global modifier stored in Preferences.Difficulty (0 = Easy, 1 = Normal, 2 = Hard).

Difficulty Incoming damage Creature health Easy ×0.7 ×0.85 Normal ×1.0 ×1.0 Hard ×1.3 ×1.2 
// Scripts/Core/Settings.cs
public static float IncomingDamageMultiplier => Difficulty switch
{
    0 => 0.7f,
    2 => 1.3f,
    _ => 1f
};

Add a fourth difficulty by extending both switches and the clamp in SetDifficulty.

docs.title: Save compatibility
docs.text:
Changing ids breaks saves

Save data stores ids, not references. Renaming or removing a weapon, rite, heirloom, attire, omen, trait or sanctum id invalidates existing saves that reference it. Adding new entries is always safe.

If you must rename an id, add a mapping in HarvestSaveSystem.Migrate() that rewrites the old id to the new one before the rest of the repair pass runs.

docs.title: A tuning workflow
docs.text:
1. Change one value.
  2. Enter Play mode, not the built player — iteration is faster.
  3. Use the smoke test for regression: .\Tools\build.ps1 -RunSmoke exercises every system and fails on exceptions.
  4. Keep a note of the value you changed; the template ships no balance spreadsheet.

docs.title: Input & rebinding
docs.text: Input runs on the Unity Input System. The template uses two layers: a small rebindable action table and a set of fixed keys read directly from Keyboard.current.

docs.title: The rebindable layer
docs.text:
Scripts/Core/Controls.cs defines the actions and their defaults:

public enum Action
{
    Attack, Dodge, Interact, Build, Companions, Inventory, Map, Quest,
    Mute, Save, Load, Potion, Rite, Bomb
}

static readonly Key[] Defaults =
{
    Key.Space, Key.LeftShift, Key.E, Key.B, Key.F, Key.I, Key.C, Key.J,
    Key.M, Key.F5, Key.F9, Key.H, Key.X, Key.G
};
Action Default Attack Space Dodge Left Shift Interact E Build B Companions F Inventory I Map C Quest J Mute M Save F5 Load F9 Potion H Rite X Bomb G

Bindings persist in PlayerPrefs under choth_bind_<index>. Reading is lazy — Load() runs on first access.

if (Bindings.Pressed(Bindings.Action.Attack)) player.Attack();
if (Bindings.Held(Bindings.Action.Dodge))    /* ... */;

Pressed returns true on the frame the key goes down; Held returns true while it is held. Both are safe when no keyboard is connected.

docs.title: Add a rebindable action
docs.text:
1. Add the member to the Action enum.
  2. Add the default Key at the same index in Defaults.

That is all — the persistence loop iterates over Defaults.Length, so the new action is stored and rebindable automatically.

docs.title: Change or reset bindings
docs.text:
Bindings.SetKey(Bindings.Action.Attack, Key.Q);
Bindings.ResetDefaults();

The Preferences → Controls screen calls these; it is built in Hud.cs.

docs.title: The fixed layer
docs.text:
These are read directly and are not rebindable, because they are tied to a specific screen or mode:

Input Action Where W A S D / arrows Move PlayerController.Update Q / Z Cycle armament / rite HarvestGame.Update K Catalog codex (hub only) HarvestGame.Update R Manage nearby sanctum (hub only) HarvestGame.Update F12 Photo mode HarvestGame.Update Esc Pause / close HarvestGame.Update, HarvestHud.Update 1–6 Menu choice HarvestHud.Update

To make one of these rebindable, add it to Bindings.Action and replace the direct kb.someKey.wasPressedThisFrame check with Bindings.Pressed(Bindings.Action.YourAction).

docs.title: Gamepad
docs.text:
PlayerController and HarvestGame read Gamepad.current when a controller is connected:

Input Action Left stick / D-pad Move South Attack East Dodge West Interact North Build Right shoulder Rite Left shoulder Bomb Start Pause D-pad up/down, South/East Menus

Gamepad bindings are fixed in code. The cleanest way to make them configurable is to extend Bindings with an input-source abstraction rather than duplicating the checks.

docs.title: Pointer input
docs.text: The UI is uGUI and uses EventSystem raycasts for mouse clicks on menus. The world itself is keyboard/gamepad only; there is no click-to-move. Placement mode uses the cursor position projected onto the ground plane (HarvestGame.HandlePlacementInput).

docs.title: Rebranding the template
docs.text: Chosen of the Harvest keeps its identity in four places: Unity's player settings, one C# namespace, the localisation table, and the persistence keys that name saves and preferences. No prefab, material or scene asset carries the name, so rebranding is a short mechanical pass rather than an asset hunt. This page is the checklist, followed by the order that avoids breaking builds and saves.

docs.title: The rebranding map
docs.text:
Every identity string a player, reviewer or build machine can actually see.

What it affects Where it lives Shipped value Window title and save folder ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset → productName ChosenOfTheHarvest Publisher / company same file → companyName, plus BuildGame.ConfigureProduct() ChosenOfTheHarvest Bundle identifier same file → applicationIdentifier: Standalone com.chosenoftheharvest.template Version string bundleVersion, HarvestGame.Version, BuildGame.Version 1.0.0 Runtime namespace 37 files with namespace ChosenOfTheHarvest ChosenOfTheHarvest Editor namespace 2 files with namespace ChosenOfTheHarvest.EditorTools ChosenOfTheHarvest.EditorTools Editor menu [MenuItem("Chosen of the Harvest/…")] in BuildGame.cs Chosen of the Harvest Title, subtitle, prologue Resources/Localization/en.json → title.* CHOSEN OF THE HARVEST Lore noun en.json → 9 values containing Harvesthold Harvesthold Pseudo-locale Resources/Localization/xx.json same strings with ?XX? Preference keys choth_settings_, choth_bind_, choth_audio_muted, choth_active_save_slot choth_ prefix Save files save_auto.json, save_slot_1..3.json, save.json, Photos/ see HarvestSaveSystem Window size HarvestGame.Awake() 1600 × 900, windowed

Display names are already data

Sanctums, traits, quests and menu labels are looked up through Lexicon and fall back to English literals in code. Changing a display name is an en.json edit; changing a type name is a code change and a save-compatibility change. Keep the two separate.

docs.title: Step 1 — Set the player identity
docs.text:
BuildGame.ConfigureProduct() rewrites companyName, productName and bundleVersion on every build, so editing ProjectSettings.asset alone is not durable if you build through the template menus.

  1. Open ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset and edit the identity block.
  2. Edit the same values in Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Editor/BuildGame.cs.
  3. Leave applicationIdentifier alone for now — the build helper never touches it.
# ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset
companyName: YourStudio
productName: YourGame
bundleVersion: 0.1.0
applicationIdentifier:
  Standalone: com.yourstudio.yourgame

// Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Editor/BuildGame.cs
public const string ProductName = "YourGame";
public const string Version = "0.1.0";

static void ConfigureProduct()
{
    PlayerSettings.companyName = "YourStudio";
    PlayerSettings.productName = ProductName;
    PlayerSettings.bundleVersion = Version;
    PlayerSettings.SetApplicationIdentifier(
        BuildTargetGroup.Standalone, "com.yourstudio.yourgame");
    // ... existing backend / window settings
}

productName is also the folder name under %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow, so a space is legal but annoying in bug reports. Prefer no spaces.

The window size is set twice

PlayerSettings.defaultScreenWidth/Height (1280 × 720) only affects the standalone launch. HarvestGame.Awake() then calls Screen.SetResolution(1600, 900, FullScreenMode.Windowed), which wins while the game runs. Change both or the player will resize itself on start.

docs.title: Step 2 — Rename the namespace
docs.text:
The runtime namespace is one identifier; the editor namespace is a child of it. Rename both with your IDE's Rename namespace refactor, not with a text replace.

// before
namespace ChosenOfTheHarvest { /* 37 runtime files */ }
namespace ChosenOfTheHarvest.EditorTools { /* ArtImporter.cs, BuildGame.cs */ }

// after
namespace YourStudio.YourGame { /* … */ }
namespace YourStudio.YourGame.EditorTools { /* … */ }

The child namespace keeps working because C# resolves parent namespaces automatically. Any using ChosenOfTheHarvest; must be renamed too — the IDE refactor does that for you.

A blanket text replace breaks the scene path

BuildGame.ScenePath is the literal "Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Scenes/ChosenOfTheHarvest.unity". A naive find-and-replace of ChosenOfTheHarvest rewrites that folder path and the editor can no longer find the bootstrap scene. Either leave the folder name alone (recommended) or move the folder and update ScenePath, ProjectSettings/EditorBuildSettings.asset and every .meta alongside it.

The CLI entry point embeds the namespace, so update any build script that calls it:

# before: -executeMethod ChosenOfTheHarvest.EditorTools.BuildGame.BuildPlayer
$unity = "C:\Program Files\Unity\Hub\Editor\6000.6.6f1\Editor\Unity.exe"

& $unity -batchmode -quit -projectPath (Get-Location) `
  -executeMethod YourStudio.YourGame.EditorTools.BuildGame.BuildPlayer `
  -logFile build.log

If the string and the namespace disagree, Unity exits with executeMethod class not found before compiling a single player.

docs.title: Step 3 — Retitle the title screen
docs.text:
HarvestGame asks Lexicon for title.name and only uses the uppercase literal as a fallback. Editing the JSON is enough; no recompile is needed after a domain reload.

{
  "key": "title.name",
  "value": "YOUR GAME"
},
{
  "key": "title.subtitle",
  "value": "A HAND-BUILT SAGA"
},
{
  "key": "title.prologue.2",
  "value": "Gather a harvest. Grow your sanctuary. Break the three wardens."
}
  1. Edit the eleven title.* entries in en.json.
  2. Mirror them in xx.json (keep the ?XX? prefix) or the pseudo-locale toggle shows the old brand.
  3. Search en.json for Harvesthold and rewrite the nine values that mention it.
  4. Reload the scene and check the title, the pause header and the prologue dialogue.

Duplicate key in the shipped table

en.json contains two entries for menu.assign.title. Lexicon keeps the last one it reads, so edit or delete both. A duplicate you forget will quietly override your new string.

docs.title: Step 4 — Re-prefix persistence (optional)
docs.text:
Four constants own the whole PlayerPrefs surface:

// Settings.cs
const string Prefix = "choth_settings_";
// Controls.cs
static readonly string Prefix = "choth_bind_";
// AudioManager.cs
const string MutePref = "choth_audio_muted";
// SaveSystem.cs
const string ActiveSlotPref = "choth_active_save_slot";

Renaming them gives your players a clean slate: old preferences and the remembered save slot are simply ignored. Existing save files are unaffected, because their names are separate literals (save_auto.json, save_slot_{n}.json).

Rebrand, then migrate once

If you want a new prefix without losing settings, read the old key, write the new one, then delete the old one on first launch. Doing it in Preferences.Load() and Bindings.Load() is enough — both already run before anything reads a value.

docs.title: Step 5 — Decide what not to rename
docs.text:
Don't rename Why HarvestSaveData field names JsonUtility maps JSON by field name; a rename silently zeroes that field SanctumType members Saves store type.ToString(); a rename turns a Farm into a fallback shrine ArmamentDef.Id, rite ids, omen ids Stored in weaponType, riteType, omens[]; unknown ids fall back or vanish Resources/Art, Resources/Audio Hard-coded in Resources.Load calls throughout The choth_ prefixes mid-project Orphans every tester's bindings, volume and active slot

Renaming the classes (HarvestGame, HarvestHud, HarvestState) is safe for saves — the type name is not serialised — but it touches hundreds of call sites for no player-visible gain. Rebrand the strings, not the vocabulary.

docs.title: Step 6 — Verify the rebrand
docs.text:
1. Press Play: title, subtitle and prologue show the new name.
  2. Open Preferences → confirm the header and any choth_ migration behaved.
  3. Build with BuildGame.BuildPlayer and check the window title and Build/ output name.
  4. Launch the player and confirm the save folder is %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\YourStudio\YourGame.
  5. Save, quit, relaunch, continue — the slot summary should still list the day and act.
  6. Run rg -n "Chosen of the Harvest|ChosenOfTheHarvest" Assets ProjectSettings and confirm every remaining hit is intentional (folder names, class names).

docs.title: Rebinding
docs.text:
Bindings for the actions in Bindings.Action are stored in PlayerPrefs under the prefix choth_bind_ and can be changed in Preferences → Controls.

// Read the current binding
Key key = Bindings.GetKey(Bindings.Action.Attack);

// Rebind
Bindings.SetKey(Bindings.Action.Attack, Key.Q);

// Restore every default
Bindings.ResetDefaults();

Bindings.Pressed(action) returns true on the frame the key goes down; Bindings.Held(action) returns true while it is held. Both no-op safely when no keyboard is present.

Fixed vs rebindable

Movement, Q, Z, K, R, F12, the menu digits and Esc are deliberately fixed because they are tied to screen layout or to a mode. Everything else is rebindable.
