docs.title: HUD and menus
docs.text: Every pixel of the interface is built at runtime with uGUI: HarvestHud owns the on-screen layers, and HarvestGame builds each screen by filling one reusable six-row menu. There are no prefabs, no canvas assets and no scene wiring — which is why a menu is added by writing a method rather than by dragging a panel.

docs.title: What is on screen
docs.text:
HarvestHud.Build() creates a Canvas (ScreenSpaceOverlay, sorting order 100) with a CanvasScaler set to ScaleWithScreenSize, reference 1920×1080, match 0.5. All text draws through UiFont — LegacyRuntime.ttf, with a dynamic OS font as the fallback — plus a hard Shadow offset of (2, -2).

Element Built by Placement Notes Day and phase Build() top-left, 30 pt Day 12 • Dusk Health bar BuildHealthBar() 300×20 at (28, -58) red, turns orange below 35% Warden bar BuildWardenBar() 560×52, top centre hidden until ShowWarden Minimap BuildMinimapShell() 330×170, top-right hidden outside expeditions Resources Build() 24 pt at (28, -92) wood, stone, pearls, food Companions Build() 24 pt at (28, -128) grace, count, omens, creed Items Build() 20 pt at (28, -164) meals, herbs, medicine, potions, rite Status line Build() 20 pt at (28, -198) HarvestGame.StatusLine Prompt Build() 26 pt, bottom y = 92 contextual E hint Toast Build() 28 pt, bottom y = 150 gold, 3.2 s default FPS Build() 20 pt, top-right off by default Menu BuildMenu() full-screen overlay six rows, title and hint Fade BuildFade() full-screen black 0.35 s flash

The status line is the hub/expedition switch. In the hub it reports creed, hymn count, act, devotion and the current quest title; inside an expedition it reports biome, floor, room type, keys, husk count and the run curse:

StatusLine = mode == Mode.Expedition
    ? $"DUNGEON   •   {ExpeditionRef.BiomeName}   •   floor {ExpeditionRef.Floor}/{ExpeditionRef.FloorCount}   " +
      $"•   {ExpeditionRef.RoomTypeLabel}   •   keys {ExpeditionRef.Keys}   " +
      $"•   {ExpeditionRef.CreatureCount} husks   •   {HarvestState.CurseName}"
    : $"{HarvestState.CreedSummary()}   •   hymn {HarvestState.Data.hymns}   •   act {Mathf.Min(CampaignStage + 1, 3)}/3   " +
      $"•   devotion {HarvestState.Data.devotion}   •   {SagaSystem.CurrentTitle}";

Refresh() runs every frame and re-reads the model, so a change made anywhere in the game shows up without an explicit update call. That includes localization: the HUD is the fastest way to see a language switch take effect.

docs.title: The minimap
docs.text: SetMinimap(rooms, current) rebuilds the panel from the floor plan each room. Connectors are drawn first as 2 px lines, then 22×22 nodes on a 56×48 px grid. Visited rooms show a type letter and colour (E entrance, C combat, L elite, T treasure, S shop, K curse, P puzzle, B Warden); unvisited rooms show ? on a dark tile. The current room gets a 30×30 gold outline behind its node.

docs.title: The Warden bar
docs.text: ShowWarden(Creature enemy) shows the bar and HideWarden() clears it. Refresh() also hides the bar when the creature is dead or inactive, and hides the whole minimap when HarvestGame.InExpedition is false. The name comes from ExpeditionRef.WardenName, uppercased, with hud.boss.unknown as the fallback.

docs.title: The title screen
docs.text:
HarvestGame.Awake() ends with OpenTitleScreen() unless the build was launched with -smoke. The title is just a menu with gameplay hidden:

bool hasSave = HarvestSaveSystem.SlotExists(HarvestSaveSystem.ActiveSlot);
string continueLine = Lexicon.Get("title.continue", "Continue") + "   •   " +
                      (hasSave
                          ? HarvestSaveSystem.SlotSummary(HarvestSaveSystem.ActiveSlot)
                          : Lexicon.Get("title.empty", "No save yet"));
Row Action New game StartNewGame() — resets HarvestState, respawns the court, shows the prologue Continue ContinueGame() — loads ActiveSlot, or toasts "No save yet" and reopens Load game ShowSaveSlots(true) Preferences ShowPreferences(0) Quit Application.Quit()

The title name and subtitle are title.name and title.subtitle. Esc on the title reopens it (the choice < 0 branch), so there is no state to fall out of.

docs.title: The pause menu
docs.text:
Esc or the gamepad Start button calls OpenPause(), which refuses while already paused, in photo mode, during a ceremony, or while placing a building. It stops time, locks input and shows six rows:

Row Action Resume ResumeGame() Save game ShowSaveSlots(false) Load game ShowSaveSlots(true) Preferences ShowPreferences() Photo mode EnterPhotoMode() Quit to title OpenTitleScreen() (the pause.quit label; the code's fallback reads "Quit to desktop")

The title is PAUSED • v1.0.0, using HarvestGame.Version, and the hint is Press 1-6 • Esc resumes. Quit returns to the title screen rather than closing the application.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
ShowPreferences(int page = 0) is three pages of ordinary menu rows. Audio and motion live on page 0, display and saving on page 1, gameplay and controls on page 2.

Page Title Rows 0 SETTINGS master, music, SFX, screen shake, reduced motion, More options 1 SETTINGS • MORE UI scale, fullscreen, FPS counter, autosave, Gameplay and controls, Back 2 SETTINGS • GAMEPLAY difficulty, language, high contrast, rebind keys, Back

Page 0 and page 1 titles are localized; page 2's title is a hard-coded English string ("SETTINGS • GAMEPLAY"), as are the difficulty, language and high-contrast row labels.

Rows toggle or cycle in place and rebuild the same page, so a click never closes the menu:

Row Control Volumes CycleVolume — 0% to 100% in 10% steps UI scale CycleScale — 0.8 to 1.3 in 0.1 steps Difficulty (Difficulty + 1) % 3 — Easy, Normal, Hard Language en ↔ xx Everything else boolean toggle

Every change calls Preferences.Save() (inside the setter) and usually Preferences.Apply(), which pushes volumes to SoundDirector, scale/FPS/contrast to the HUD, fullscreen mode to Screen, and the locale to Lexicon.

docs.title: Rebinding
docs.text: ShowRebindMenu(page) is three pages over the fourteen keyboard actions: attack, dodge, interact, rite, bomb; then potion, build, companions, inventory, map; then quest log, mute, quick save, quick load. Choosing a row calls BeginRebind, which hides the menu and sets the prompt to Press a key • Esc cancels. HandleRebind captures the next key press, writes it through Bindings.SetKey, and returns to the same page.

docs.title: Toasts, prompts and dialogue
docs.text:
A toast is one Text with a countdown:

public void Toast(string text, float seconds = 3.2f)
{
    toastText.text = text;
    toastTimer = seconds;
}

The timer is decremented with Time.deltaTime in Update, so toasts freeze while the game is paused and resume on unpause. HarvestGame.Toast(string) forwards to this method, which is why every system can toast without holding a HUD reference.

Prompts are simpler: SetPrompt(text) replaces the line at the bottom of the screen, and UpdatePrompt() in HarvestGame decides what to show based on what the player is standing next to.

Dialogue is a menu, not a panel. ShowDialogue(speaker, lines, onDone) shows one line at a time with a Continue row, and swaps the second row for npc.leave on the last line. Closing the menu with Esc also fires onDone, which is how the prologue unpauses the game.

docs.title: Photo mode
docs.text:
EnterPhotoMode() hides the HUD and every companion name tag, stops time and locks input. The camera detaches from the player and pans over the scene:

Input Effect W A S D or arrows pan the focus point at 6 units/s, clamped to the world Mouse scroll zoom between 4 and 16 units F12 capture Esc exit to the pause menu

CapturePhoto() waits for WaitForEndOfFrame, reads the screen into a Texture2D, and writes a PNG:

string directory = Path.Combine(Application.persistentDataPath, "Photos");
Directory.CreateDirectory(directory);
string path = Path.Combine(directory, "photo_" + System.DateTime.Now.ToString("yyyyMMdd_HHmmss") + ".png");
File.WriteAllBytes(path, texture.EncodeToPNG());

The file name is timestamped to the second, so two captures in the same second overwrite each other. ExitPhotoMode() restores the HUD and name tags and reopens the pause menu.

docs.title: The full-screen menus
docs.text:
All of these are ShowMenu calls, so they share navigation, the dark overlay and the numbered rows. Keys are the defaults from Bindings and the fixed Update branches.

Key Screen Method Availability I Inventory and equipment ShowInventory() hub K Catalog (weapons, omens, heirlooms, equipment, buildings, enemies) ShowCatalogMenu() hub F Companion roster ShowCompanionRoster() hub C Pilgrimage map ShowCampaignMap() hub J Quest log ShowQuestLog() anywhere B Build menu ShowBuildMenu() / ShowInteriorBuildMenu() hub or interior R Sanctum menu for the nearest building ShowSanctumMenu(building) hub, within 2.4 units E Interact — altar, portal, NPC, node Interact() context

Long lists page rather than scroll. The catalog and the roster show five rows plus a Next/Previous row; when everything fits on one page, that sixth row is simply unused.

Six rows is the hard limit

HarvestHud allocates exactly six option texts and six icon slots. A ShowMenu call with more than six strings silently drops the extras, and every screen above is designed around that cap (five rows plus paging). Raise the array size in BuildMenu before adding a seventh row.

docs.title: Keyboard and gamepad navigation
docs.text:
HarvestHud.HandleMenuInput() runs only while a menu is open:

Input Result 1 … 6 choose that row Esc close with -1 (cancel) Gamepad d-pad up/down move the highlight Gamepad left stick up/down move the highlight Gamepad South (A) confirm the highlighted row Gamepad East (B) cancel Gamepad Start open the pause menu (from HarvestGame.Update)

The highlight is a colour swap to (1, 0.86, 0.4) on the selected row, and MoveMenuSelection skips rows that are inactive, so paged menus cannot land on an empty slot.

Every visible row is prefixed with its number (1) Resume), which is why the hints read Press 1-6. ShowMenu also sets HarvestGame.InputLocked = true and HideMenu/Close clears it, so world input is off for as long as a menu is up.

A keyboard is required to drive menus

HandleMenuInput starts with var kb = Keyboard.current; if (kb == null) return; before it reads the gamepad. On a device with a gamepad and no keyboard recognised by the Input System, menus render but cannot be navigated. Add a null-safe path for kb if you ship to such a device.

docs.title: Accessibility and display
docs.text:
Four options change the HUD rather than the game:

Option Applied by Effect UI scale SetUiScale CanvasScaler.scaleFactor, clamped 0.8-1.3 High contrast SetHighContrast gold prompt, near-white status, pale green items, near-black menu FPS counter SetFpsVisible shows the smoothed top-right counter Reduced motion Preferences.ReducedMotion Shake and HitStop return immediately

High contrast deliberately touches only the prompt, status, item and menu background — the day line, resource line, health bar and boss bar keep their colours. If you extend it, SetHighContrast is the single place to do it.

public void SetUiScale(float scale)
{
    if (canvasScaler != null) canvasScaler.scaleFactor = Mathf.Clamp(scale, 0.8f, 1.3f);
}

The FPS readout uses unscaled time and an exponential smooth, so it keeps updating while the game is paused but only if it is visible:

float instant = Time.unscaledDeltaTime > 0f ? 1f / Time.unscaledDeltaTime : 60f;
fpsSmooth = Mathf.Lerp(fpsSmooth, instant, 0.08f);
fpsText.text = Mathf.RoundToInt(fpsSmooth) + " " + Lexicon.Get("hud.fps", "FPS");

docs.title: Localization
docs.text: Lexicon is a small static table that loads one JSON file from Resources/Localization and answers Get(key, fallback) calls from it. English ships as en.json, and xx.json is a pseudo-locale that prefixes every string with ?XX? so layout problems are impossible to miss. Both files hold the same 349 entries, and adding a language is a new JSON file plus one line in the settings picker.

docs.title: The two tables
docs.text:
Each file is a single object with an entries array, which maps directly onto the Table and Entry classes JsonUtility deserialises:

{
  "entries": [
    {
      "key": "campaign.title",
      "value": "PILGRIMAGE MAP"
    },
    {
      "key": "quest.buildfarm",
      "value": "Plant a Rose Garden"
    }
  ]
}

[Serializable]
class Entry
{
    public string key;
    public string value;
}

[Serializable]
class Table
{
    public Entry[] entries;
}
File Entries Unique keys Purpose en.json 349 348 shipped English xx.json 349 348 pseudo-locale for layout testing

The count differs from the key count by one because menu.assign.title appears twice — once as ASSIGN, once as ASSIGN {0}. The loader assigns in file order, so the second value wins and Lexicon.KeyCount reports 348.

docs.title: Reading a string
docs.text:
Two methods cover every call in the project. Neither throws.

public static string Get(string key, string fallback = null)
{
    Load();
    if (key != null && Values.TryGetValue(key, out var value)) return value;
    return fallback ?? key;
}

public static string Format(string key, string fallback, params object[] args)
{
    string template = Get(key, fallback);
    try
    {
        return string.Format(template, args);
    }
    catch (FormatException)
    {
        return template;
    }
}
Situation Get returns key present in the loaded table the table value key absent, fallback supplied the fallback key absent, no fallback the key itself key == null, no fallback null Situation Format returns template has matching {0}… slots the formatted string template has no slots the template, arguments ignored template has a malformed slot the raw template (the exception is caught)

The practical rule: always pass a fallback. It is what the player sees if a translator misses a key, and it doubles as the readable default in code review. The fallback is the C# string, not the English table — a missing German entry shows the source-language fallback, never en.json.

Format is used wherever a number or name is spliced in, for example the HUD resource line:

resourceText.text = Lexicon.Format("hud.resources",
    "Wood {0}     Stone {1}     Pearls {2}     Food {3}",
    data.wood, data.stone, data.pearls, data.food);

docs.title: Key families
docs.text:
Keys are dotted and grouped by screen or system, which makes a missing translation easy to locate.

Prefix Entries Examples menu. 36 menu.companions.title, menu.next, menu.assign.title dungeon. 31 floor, key and room copy shop. 22 stock lines and prices campaign. 21 campaign.act1, campaign.cleared, campaign.victory.title building. 20 building.farm ("Rose Garden"), building.temple ("Grand Temple") prompt. 19 contextual E prompts companion. 17 actions, blessings, costs npc. 16 Oracle intro plus one hint per quest stage settings. 15 every row and On/Off slots. 14 save-slot labels and toasts title. 11 title screen and prologue quest. 11 nine stage titles, quest.title, quest.reward ceremony. 10 the six altar options and their results hud. 7 hud.day, hud.fps, hud.resources, hud.boss.unknown

Smaller families follow the same pattern: trait., room., mood., recipe., meta., daily., pause., rebind., phase., creed., priority., act., forge., curse. and a single photo.prompt.

Four families are addressed dynamically, so adding content adds keys without touching the loader:

// Building.cs
return Lexicon.Get("building." + Type.ToString().ToLowerInvariant(), fallback);

// DayCycle.cs
Lexicon.Get("phase." + Phases[PhaseIndex].ToLowerInvariant(), Phases[PhaseIndex]);

// FloorPlan.cs
return Lexicon.Get("room." + type.ToString().ToLowerInvariant(), fallback);

// FollowerCatalog.cs
Lexicon.Get("trait." + trait.ToString().ToLowerInvariant(), trait.ToString());

A new SanctumType.Beehive needs building.beehive in every locale; if you forget, the enum name appears in the UI instead of the pretty label.

docs.title: The pseudo-locale
docs.text:
xx.json is a full copy of en.json with every value prefixed by ?XX? and identical keys. It exists to stress the layout without a real translation:

  • Every string grows by five characters, which exposes labels that only fit at English length.
  • Every string is visibly fake, so a hard-coded literal stands out next to the prefixed ones.
  • Because the keys are identical, KeyCount should still report 348 — a lower number means the pseudo file drifted.

It is selected from Settings → Gameplay → Language, which shows Pseudo (layout) when the preference is xx and English otherwise.

Ship with xx disabled, not deleted

Leaving xx.json in the project costs one TextAsset and makes it trivial to re-check a new screen for clipping. If you remove it, remove the picker branch too, or choosing the second language silently falls back to every fallback string in code.

docs.title: Hot switching
docs.text:
There is no scene reload. The locale is a string, the cache is a dictionary, and the next Get after a switch reloads the table:

public static void SetLocale(string next)
{
    if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(next)) return;
    locale = next;
    loaded = false;
    Values.Clear();
}

static void Load()
{
    if (loaded) return;
    loaded = true;
    Values.Clear();

    var asset = Resources.Load<TextAsset>("Localization/" + locale);
    if (asset == null) return;
    // …JsonUtility.FromJson<Table>…
}

Preferences.Apply() calls Lexicon.SetLocale(Language) for you, and ShowPreferences calls SetLocale directly when the language row is pressed so the menu redraws immediately.

What refreshes instantly and what does not:

Element After a switch HUD lines, prompts, toasts next frame — Refresh() re-reads every Lexicon.Format call The settings menu immediate — the row rebuilds itself after the change Any other open menu keeps its old text until it is closed and reopened Already-spawned labels, dialogue lines unchanged; they were resolved once at spawn time

Because Load() is lazy, a switch costs one Resources load on the next Get, not at the moment of the click.

A missing file is silent

If Resources/Localization/<locale>.json does not exist or is not imported as a TextAsset, Load() returns with an empty dictionary and no error. Lexicon.Locale still reports the requested id, so the only symptom is a screen full of C# fallbacks. Check Lexicon.KeyCount — 0 means the file never loaded.

docs.title: Adding a language
docs.text:
1. Copy en.json to a new two-letter name, for example de.json, in Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Resources/Localization/.

2. Translate the value fields only. Keys, order and placeholder tokens must survive untouched:

{
  "key": "hud.day",
  "value": "Tag {0}"
}

Dropping or renumbering {0} does not crash anything — Format catches the FormatException and returns the unformatted template — but the player sees the braces.

3. Leave the key set complete. There is no fallback chain between locales, so every key you omit shows the C# fallback string in the middle of translated UI. Diff the key lists before shipping:

$a = (Get-Content en.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).entries.key
$b = (Get-Content de.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).entries.key
Compare-Object $a $b

4. Extend the picker. The shipped settings page is a two-way toggle, so it only knows en and xx:

case 1:
    Preferences.SetLanguage(Preferences.Language == "en" ? "xx" : "en");

    Lexicon.SetLocale(Preferences.Language);
    ShowPreferences(2);
    break;

Replace it with a cycle over the locales you ship, for example en → xx → de → en, and update the label on the same row (which is currently the hard-coded "Language • ..." string in ShowPreferences).

5. Persist and apply. Preferences.SetLanguage writes choth_settings_language; Preferences.Apply() re-pushes the locale on boot:

public static void Apply()
{
    Load();
    // …audio, HUD, fullscreen…
    Lexicon.SetLocale(Language);
}

6. Verify in play. Load the language, open the quest log, the settings pages and a build menu, and check that Lexicon.KeyCount matches the source table. Because the HUD refreshes every frame, a missing key is visible immediately as a code-style fallback string among translated text.

Locale ids are filenames

SetLocale("de") loads Resources/Localization/de.json. An id like de-DE works only if the file is named de-DE.json; there is no region fallback from de-DE to de.

docs.title: Quests and the campaign
docs.text: SagaSystem runs a nine-stage chain that walks a new Sovereign from the first Rose Garden to the death of the third Warden. Every stage is a question asked about the save file rather than an event you have to remember to raise, so a quest can never get stuck waiting for a callback that was never sent. Press J at any point to read the log.

docs.title: The nine-stage chain
docs.text:
The English copy below is exactly what ships in en.json; the condition column is the code that decides the stage is finished. Stage numbers are the value of HarvestState.Data.questStage.

Stage Quest key Objective (English copy) Completes when Devotion 0 quest.buildfarm Plant a Rose Garden a Sanctum with Type == SanctumType.Farm exists +2 1 quest.hymn Hold a hymn at the Harvest Altar HarvestState.Data.hymns > 0 +2 2 quest.reflection Defeat the Gilded Stag in the Ashen Orchard campaignStage >= 1 +2 3 quest.forest Defeat the Mire Queen in the Drowned Conservatory campaignStage >= 2 +2 4 quest.temple Defeat the Obsidian Sultan in the Ember Citadel campaignStage >= 3 +4 5 quest.sanctum Raise the Grand Temple a Sanctum with Type == SanctumType.Temple exists +4 6 quest.companions Grow the flock to eight HarvestState.Data.companions >= 8 +4 7 quest.devotion Reach 30 Devotion HarvestState.Data.devotion >= 30 +4 8 quest.done The Harvesthold has endured all three wardens. terminal — Stage >= FinalStage —

Two details are easy to miss when reading the copy alone:

  • The first stage says Rose Garden because that is the localized label of SanctumType.Farm (building.farm), not a separate building type.
  • Stage 5 asks for a Grand Temple (building.temple) after the third Warden. It is a post-victory build target, not a gate on the campaign.

docs.title: How a stage advances
docs.text:
HarvestGame.Update() polls the chain once a second, and only in the hub while input is unlocked:

if (mode == Mode.Hub && !InputLocked)
{
    questTimer -= Time.deltaTime;
    if (questTimer <= 0f)
    {
        questTimer = 1f;
        SagaSystem.Evaluate(this);
    }
}

Evaluate is a while loop, so several stages can fall in a single pass:

while (Stage < FinalStage)
{
    bool done = Stage switch
    {
        0 => HasFarm(boot),
        1 => HarvestState.Data.hymns > 0,
        2 => HarvestState.Data.campaignStage >= 1,
        3 => HarvestState.Data.campaignStage >= 2,
        4 => HarvestState.Data.campaignStage >= 3,
        5 => HasTemple(boot),
        6 => HarvestState.Data.companions >= 8,
        7 => HarvestState.Data.devotion >= 30,
        _ => true
    };

    if (!done) break;

    HarvestState.Data.questStage++;
    int reward = Stage >= 5 ? 4 : 2;
    HarvestState.Data.devotion += reward;
    HarvestState.NotifyChanged();
    boot.Toast(string.Format(Lexicon.Get("quest.reward", "Quest complete • +{0} devotion"), reward));
    SoundDirector.Sfx("ui", 0.65f, 1.15f);
}

Finish a Grand Temple while already holding eight companions and thirty Devotion and the loop completes stages 5, 6 and 7 in the same second, paying each reward separately.

Evaluate is also called from two event-driven places so the player does not have to wait for the next poll:

  • HarvestGame.WardenDefeated(int act, string bossName), after it raises campaignStage.
  • The end of HarvestGame.CeremonyRoutine, which is where a Hymn increments HarvestState.Data.hymns.

Stage is clamped to FinalStage on read, so a corrupt or hand-edited questStage of 999 still reads as complete instead of throwing.

docs.title: Rewards and devotion
docs.text:
Devotion is the only currency the chain pays. The payout is decided by the new stage value, because Stage is a property read after questStage++.

Stages completed New stage Devotion per stage Subtotal 0-3 1-4 2 8 4-7 5-8 4 16 Total 24

The campaign pays on top of that. WardenDefeated awards Mathf.RoundToInt((8 + act * 4) * (HasHeirloom("crown") ? 1.15f : 1f)), which is the boss rewards 8/12/16 line in JourneyPacing.BalanceLine:

Act Index Base devotion With the Crown heirloom Ashen Orchard 0 8 9 Drowned Conservatory 1 12 14 Ember Citadel 2 16 18

Devotion sinks are in HarvestGame.ShowMetaUpgrades(). Each track caps at level 3 and costs its base plus 2 per level already bought:

Track First cost What it buys Vitality 3 HarvestState.MaxHealth gains metaVitality * 15 Wrath 3 HarvestState.WeaponDamage gains metaWrath * 4 Provisions 2 +10 food and +5 meals per level Charisma 2 +3 loyalty to every companion per level

Devotion is permanent

campaignStage, questStage, devotion and the four meta* levels all live in the save file. Clearing Act III does not reset the chain, and the upgrade menu reads the same devotion the quest rewards paid into.

docs.title: The quest log
docs.text:
J calls HarvestGame.ShowQuestLog(), which is a four-row ShowMenu rather than a bespoke panel:

public void ShowQuestLog()
{
    HarvestHudRef.ShowMenu(Lexicon.Get("quest.title", "QUEST LOG"),
        new[]
        {
            SagaSystem.CurrentLine,
            SagaSystem.CompletedLine,
            SagaSystem.ProgressLine,
            Lexicon.Get("campaign.close", "Close")
        }, "Esc to close", _ => { });
}
Row Built by Reads like Current SagaSystem.CurrentLine ▶ Plant a Rose Garden Completed SagaSystem.CompletedLine ✓ Plant a Rose Garden • Hold a hymn… Progress SagaSystem.ProgressLine Campaign 1/3 • Devotion 14 • 92 rooms / ~95 min Close campaign.close Close

CompletedLine returns ✓ none yet while Stage <= 0 and joins the finished titles with •. ProgressLine clamps campaignStage + 1 to 3, so it never reads 4/3. CurrentTitle looks up Keys[Stage] with a clamped index, which means an out-of-range stage shows the last key instead of blank text.

The Oracle gives the same information in dialogue. TalkToNpc picks QuestHintKeys[Stage] — one npc.hint.* line per stage — and appends npc.progress once at least one Warden is down.

docs.title: Campaign stages and act intros
docs.text:
campaignStage is not a quest counter: it is the number of Wardens broken, 0-3. HarvestGame.CampaignStage clamps it, and both the map and the HUD read that clamp.

Act Map row (campaign.act1…) Warden Rooms Devotion 0 ACT I • ASHEN ORCHARD • The Gilded Stag The Gilded Stag 20 8 1 ACT II • DROWNED CONSERVATORY • The Mire Queen The Mire Queen 32 12 2 ACT III • EMBER CITADEL • The Obsidian Sultan The Obsidian Sultan 40 16

JourneyPacing totals the three acts at 92 rooms and targets 80-120 minutes (ShortSummary reports 92 rooms / ~95 min, which is what the quest log and status line show).

C opens ShowCampaignMap() in the hub. Each act row is labelled CLEARED, AVAILABLE or LOCKED from its index against CampaignStage; choosing a locked act toasts campaign.locked.toast ("Clear the previous warden first") instead of starting it. The remaining rows are the devotion upgrades, the quest log, and Close.

Picking an available act runs ShowActIntro(act), which sets currentAct, builds act.intro — "The road to {0} opens. {1} waits at its end." — and offers two choices: Begin pilgrimage (EnterExpedition(currentAct)) or Return to the Harvesthold.

docs.title: The victory sequence
docs.text:
Victory is a flag check on the way home, not a scripted cutscene. The order is:

  1. The third Warden dies and Dungeon calls WardenDefeated(2, bossName), which sets campaignStage = 3, pays 16 devotion (18 with the Crown) and calls SagaSystem.Evaluate.
  2. The player leaves the expedition with loot; ExitExpedition(true) plays the portal, returns to the hub and calls HarvestSaveSystem.Autosave().
  3. Immediately after, ExitExpedition checks campaignStage >= 3 && !victorySeen and calls ShowVictory().
  4. ShowVictory() sets victorySeen = true, adds 10 devotion and opens the campaign.victory.title menu.
void ShowVictory()
{
    HarvestState.Data.victorySeen = true;
    HarvestState.Data.devotion += 10;
    HarvestState.NotifyChanged();
    HarvestHudRef.ShowMenu(Lexicon.Get("campaign.victory.title", "THE HARVEST ENDURES"),
        new[]
        {
            Lexicon.Get("campaign.victory.body", "All three wardens have fallen. …"),
            Lexicon.Get("campaign.victory.reward", "The harvest is eternal."),
            Lexicon.Get("campaign.close", "Close")
        }, "Press 1-3", _ => { });
}

Because victorySeen is saved, the screen shows once per save. The autosave runs before the flag is written, so the flag lands in the file on the next save (or the next successful expedition); this is harmless because ShowVictory is also gated on the live flag.

docs.title: Quest state in the save
docs.text:
There is no quest file and no quest component. The whole chain is three fields on HarvestSaveData, serialised with the rest of the state by HarvestSaveSystem:

Field Type Default Meaning questStage int 0 current stage, 0-8 campaignStage int 0 Wardens broken, 0-3 victorySeen bool false victory screen already shown hymns int 0 Hymns held; also gates stage 1 devotion int 0 reward currency and stage 7 gate

HarvestState.Reset() (called by StartNewGame) replaces Data with a fresh HarvestSaveData, which is the only thing that rewinds the chain.

Hub quests need a save

Autosave fires on a successful expedition return, not on quest completion. Farm, hymn, temple, companion and devotion stages finish in the hub and stay in memory until the next F5 or expedition. Tell players to save before quitting after a hub milestone.

docs.title: Adding your own stage
docs.text:
The chain is data-light by design, so a new stage is four edits and one localization entry. This walkthrough appends a tenth stage that asks for a Bell Tower.

1. Raise FinalStage and add the key. FinalStage is the highest valid stage, not the number of stages.

public const int FinalStage = 9;

static readonly string[] Keys =
{
    "quest.buildfarm",
    // …
    "quest.devotion",
    "quest.done",
    "quest.belltower"
};

2. Add the condition arm. Stage numbers must stay contiguous from 0.

7 => HarvestState.Data.devotion >= 30,
8 => HasBellTower(boot),
_ => true

3. Write the predicate. A Sanctum lookup is the cheapest pattern:

static bool HasBellTower(HarvestGame boot)
{
    foreach (var building in boot.Sanctums)
        if (building != null && building.Type == SanctumType.BellTower) return true;
    return false;
}

4. Add the Oracle hint. QuestHintKeys in GameBootstrap.cs must grow in lockstep or the Oracle will repeat the wrong line:

static readonly string[] QuestHintKeys =
{
    "npc.hint.farm", "npc.hint.hymn", "npc.hint.reflection",
    "npc.hint.forest", "npc.hint.temple", "npc.hint.sanctum",
    "npc.hint.companions", "npc.hint.devotion", "npc.hint.done",
    "npc.hint.belltower"
};

5. Add the strings to both en.json and xx.json:

{ "key": "quest.belltower", "value": "Raise a Bell Tower" },
{ "key": "npc.hint.belltower", "value": "A Bell Tower would call the flock home. Build one." }

Two silent failure modes

  • If you forget to raise FinalStage, the new arm is unreachable: the while loop stops at the old maximum.
  • If you forget the Keys entry, CurrentTitle clamps to Keys.Length - 1 and quietly shows the previous stage's title. Both mistakes look like "the quest never finishes" in play.

If the new stage needs state of its own, add the field to HarvestSaveData and follow the schema-bump walkthrough in Saving and loading so old saves get a sensible default.

docs.title: Saving and loading
docs.text: Chosen of the Harvest keeps three manual slots plus a dedicated autosave, all written as pretty-printed JSON with JsonUtility. Every write is atomic within the folder, every existing file is copied to .bak before it is replaced, and an old single-file save is still picked up by slot 1. Schema version 4 is the current shape; the migration pass repairs older files in place on load.

docs.title: The slot model
docs.text:
HarvestSaveSystem defines four slots, numbered 0-3:

Slot Constant File Appears in 0 AutosaveSlot save_auto.json Load menu only 1 FirstSlot save_slot_1.json Save and Load menus 2 — save_slot_2.json Save and Load menus 3 SlotCount save_slot_3.json Save and Load menus

SlotCount is 3, so the loops in ShowSaveSlots run 1..3, and Mathf.Clamp(slot, AutosaveSlot, SlotCount) guards every public entry point. The autosave is deliberately absent from the save menu so a manual save can never overwrite it — but it is the first row of the load menu.

The last slot used is remembered in PlayerPrefs under choth_active_save_slot. ActiveSlot clamps both the read and the write to 0..SlotCount, defaults to FirstSlot, and calls PlayerPrefs.Save().

A fresh install therefore continues from slot 1, and Save() with no argument writes the active slot. Only manual saves update ActiveSlot; the autosave does not steal the active slot.

docs.title: Where the files live
docs.text:
Everything sits directly in Application.persistentDataPath — Unity's per-user data folder (the LocalLow tree on Windows), with no subfolder added by the template. SlotPath(slot) builds the name: save_auto.json for slot 0, save_slot_N.json otherwise.

Path Written by Purpose save_slot_1.json … save_slot_3.json Save(1..3) manual slots save_auto.json Autosave() last successful expedition return <slot>.json.bak Save(slot) copy of the previous file <slot>.json.tmp Save(slot) transient; deleted after the copy save.json pre-slot builds legacy single save, read as slot 1

Test roots

UseTestRoot("ProofTest") repoints Root at a subfolder of persistentDataPath and clears it, so a smoke run starts clean; UseDefaultRoot() restores normal behaviour.

docs.title: What gets written
docs.text:
HarvestSaveData is one flat [Serializable] class. JsonUtility.ToJson serialises public fields only, so everything below is a field rather than a property.

Group Fields Notes Progress day, campaignStage, questStage, devotion, pilgrimages, victorySeen, npcIntroSeen, hymns quest and act state Resources wood, stone, grace, pearls, food, meals, herbs, medicine, potions, bombs clamped by HarvestState.NotifyChanged() Combat health, weaponLevel, weaponType, armorId, charmId, riteType health is written from the live player on save Creeds creedGrace, creedCombat, creedEconomy, creedMeta one id per track Meta metaVitality, metaWrath, metaProvisions, metaCharisma devotion upgrades, 0-3 World buildings (List<SanctumData>) type, position, level, rotation, dirt, condition, interior pieces Companions companions, companionRecords (List<CompanionRecord>) count plus names, traits, needs, jobs, relationships Collections attire, omens, heirlooms, memorials owned ids and grave records Versioning saveVersion, socialVersion see Schema 4

Field initialisers supply the defaults: day = 1, wood = 10, food = 8, companions = 4, health = 100, weaponType = "sword", armorId = "wool", charmId = "ember", riteType = "smite", socialVersion = 2.

docs.title: What is not persisted
docs.text: Not saved Why HarvestState.CurrentCurse, RunHealthPenalty runtime-only pilgrimage modifiers, re-rolled on entry Player world position ApplyLoadedSave() puts the player back at the altar, Stage3D.P(0f, -3f) An expedition in progress loading calls ExitExpedition(false) and rebuilds the hub Camera distance, shake, hit-stop view state, not progress UI and audio options PlayerPrefs under choth_settings_ Key bindings PlayerPrefs under choth_bind_ Active slot PlayerPrefs under choth_active_save_slot Photo-mode PNGs written next to the saves, outside the schema

docs.title: Writing a save
docs.text:
Save(int slot) is the only writer. It persists the version, reconciles the companion list, then replaces the slot in an order that leaves a usable file at every step:

public static void Save(int slot)
{
    slot = Mathf.Clamp(slot, AutosaveSlot, SlotCount);
    HarvestState.Data.saveVersion = CurrentVersion;
    HarvestState.EnsureCompanionRecords();

    string path = SlotPath(slot);
    string temp = path + ".tmp";
    string backup = path + ".bak";
    string json = JsonUtility.ToJson(HarvestState.Data, true);

    Directory.CreateDirectory(Root);
    File.WriteAllText(temp, json);
    if (File.Exists(path))
    {
        try { File.Copy(path, backup, true); }
        catch (Exception exception) { Debug.LogWarning("Save backup failed: " + exception.Message); }
    }
    File.Copy(temp, path, true);
    File.Delete(temp);

    if (slot != AutosaveSlot) ActiveSlot = slot;
    Debug.Log($"[Save] slot={slot} {path}");
}
Step Failure behaviour Write <slot>.json.tmp throws; the real file is untouched Copy <slot>.json to .bak warning only; the save continues Copy .tmp over <slot>.json throws on a locked file; .bak still holds the previous save Delete .tmp a leftover .tmp is ignored by loads and removed by Delete(slot)

Before Save runs, SaveGame() and SaveToSlotNow() copy the live values that do not write themselves back: player health, each companion's carried haul (FlushHaul()), sanctum dirt and condition (SyncSanctumState()) and the companion records (SyncCompanionRecords()).

docs.title: Loading and recovery
docs.text:
Load(int slot) has three fallbacks, in order: the legacy file, the .bak copy, and failure.

public static bool Load(int slot)
{
    slot = Mathf.Clamp(slot, AutosaveSlot, SlotCount);
    string path = SlotPath(slot);
    if (!File.Exists(path) && slot == FirstSlot && File.Exists(LegacyPath))
        path = LegacyPath;
    if (!File.Exists(path)) return false;

    if (!TryRead(path, out var loaded))
    {
        string backup = path + ".bak";
        if (!File.Exists(backup) || !TryRead(backup, out loaded))
        {
            Debug.LogError("[Load] Both save and backup failed: " + path);
            return false;
        }
        Debug.LogWarning("[Load] primary save corrupt; loaded .bak");
    }

    HarvestState.Data = loaded;
    Migrate();
    if (slot != AutosaveSlot) ActiveSlot = slot;
    HarvestState.NotifyChanged();
    return true;
}

The return value is the whole error contract — every caller toasts on false:

Caller Message on failure ContinueGame() title.empty ("No save yet") LoadFromSlot(slot) slots.missing ("That slot is empty") LoadGame() (F9) "No save found"

TryRead rejects only unreadable or blank files: it reads the text, returns false when the content is null or whitespace, parses with JsonUtility.FromJson<HarvestSaveData> and returns whether the result is non-null. Any exception is caught and logged as a warning.

One generation of backup

.bak holds the file as it was before the most recent successful write — not a history. Two bad saves in a row leave you with a backup of the first bad state. If a player reports a corrupt slot, stop playing that slot, copy save_slot_N.json.bak over save_slot_N.json, then load.

SlotSummary feeds the menus and never throws on a broken file. It returns "empty" when there is no file (with the same legacy fallback for slot 1). Otherwise it builds MM-dd HH:mm | Day N | Act N from the file timestamp and the parsed stage, clamping the act to 1..3; if the JSON will not parse it returns the timestamp alone.

docs.title: Schema version 4 and migration
docs.text:
CurrentVersion is 4 and HarvestSaveData.saveVersion defaults to 4. Save stamps the current version before serialising, so a file always records the build that wrote it. Migrate() then runs on every load, not just old files:

static void Migrate()
{
    if (HarvestState.Data.saveVersion < CurrentVersion)
    {
        if (HarvestState.Data.buildings != null)
            foreach (var building in HarvestState.Data.buildings)
            {
                if (building == null) continue;
                if (building.level < 1) building.level = 1;
                if (building.condition <= 0f) building.condition = 100f;
                if (building.interior == null) building.interior = new List<InteriorPieceData>();
            }

        HarvestState.EnsureLoadout();
        if (HarvestState.Data.companionRecords != null)
            foreach (var record in HarvestState.Data.companionRecords)
            {
                if (record == null) continue;
                if (record.inReflection < 0) record.inReflection = -1;
                record.priority = Mathf.Clamp(record.priority, 0, 2);
            }

        HarvestState.Data.saveVersion = CurrentVersion;
    }

    HarvestState.EnsureCompanionRecords();
}

There is no switch (saveVersion) with one branch per version. Migration is a single idempotent repair pass: it fixes anything that would be invalid under the current rules and moves the number forward. That keeps the code short, and it means a v1 file and a v3 file take the same path.

Repair Applies to Default it enforces building.level every SanctumData at least 1 building.condition every SanctumData 100 when non-positive building.interior every SanctumData empty list, never null armorId, charmId, riteType EnsureLoadout() a valid, owned id attire EnsureLoadout() wool, ember inReflection each CompanionRecord -1 (not in the chamber) priority each CompanionRecord clamped 0-2

EnsureCompanionRecords() handles the second version number, socialVersion, and runs unconditionally at the end of Migrate. It upgrades the relationship data in steps:

From To Backfill < 1 1 friend and partner set to -1 on every record < 2 2 parentA, parentB, childDay set to -1

It then trims or grows companionRecords to Data.companions, fills blank names and traits from CompanionCatalog, clamps needs and levels, and resolves duplicate names. A save that predates companions entirely loads with a complete court rather than a null list.

docs.title: F5, F9, and autosave
Adding a field: a worked example
docs.text:
Say you add sanctumMorale, a float that starts every sanctum at 60 and must never be 0 — a value older saves cannot contain. This is the full change set.

1. Add the field to HarvestSaveData, next to the other per-run counters:

public float sanctumMorale = 60f;

2. Bump the constant in HarvestSaveSystem:

public const int CurrentVersion = 5;

3. Repair it in Migrate(), inside the existing saveVersion < CurrentVersion block and before the stamp:

if (HarvestState.Data.sanctumMorale <= 0f)
    HarvestState.Data.sanctumMorale = 60f;

HarvestState.Data.saveVersion = CurrentVersion;

4. If the field lives on a child record, repair it in EnsureCompanionRecords() instead and raise socialVersion with a guarded block, the way friend/partner and the parent ids already do. Keep the socialVersion gate — it is what stops a repair from re-running every load.

5. Test against an old file. Load a slot written by the previous build and check the [Load] slot=… version=… log line, which reports the version after migration.

JsonUtility leaves a field that is absent from the JSON at its default value, so step 3 is not optional for any field whose 0/false/null is not a playable state. A field that is happy at zero — a counter, a flag — needs only steps 1 and 2.

Version numbers are cheap

Bump CurrentVersion even when a new field needs no repair: the number is written into each file and shows up in every [Load] log line.

docs.title: Deleting a slot
docs.text:
Delete(int slot) removes all four possible files for that slot — .json, .bak, .tmp and, when slot 1 is deleted, the legacy save.json. Each unlink is guarded by File.Exists, so deleting an empty slot is a no-op.

The pause menu reaches it through ShowDeleteSlots(), which offers slots 1-3 only and warns "Deleting is permanent". There is no undo and no confirmation step beyond that hint — the menu itself is the confirmation.

docs.title: Asset Store submission
docs.text:
This page is the packaging and listing checklist for publishing the template in the Unity Asset Store Templates category, based on the Asset Store Submission Guidelines (last updated 20 May 2026) and the Asset Store Content Transparency policy.

Not legal advice

Requirements change. Re-read the guidelines before every submission.

docs.title: What the guidelines require of a Template
docs.text:
Templates are a distinct category with extra rules (§2.6):

Rule Requirement How this template satisfies it 2.6.a Designed as an instructional, tutorial or framework product The package is a framework plus a playable demo 2.6.b Visual content or functionality demonstrated in a demo scene Scenes/ChosenOfTheHarvest.unity is the demo 2.6.c Documentation explains how the project is designed and how to extend it Offline manual in Documentation/ plus the online site 1.1.f Template submissions include demo scenes One scene, fully playable 1.3.c Templates on Unity 6.5+ must support URP or HDRP URP 17.6

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text:
One root folder, as §2.1.a requires:

Assets/
└── ChosenOfTheHarvest/
    ├── Documentation/           Markdown manual (ships)
    ├── Editor/
    ├── Resources/
    ├── Scenes/
    ├── Scripts/
    ├── Settings/
    └── Third-Party Notices.txt

Resources is nested under the root. Resources.Load finds any folder named Resources, so a single root folder does not break the load paths.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
• The demo scene plays from a clean import with zero console errors and warnings originating from package content (§1.1.b).
  • No duplicate, unused or redundant files (§2.1.c).
  • No AssetStoreTools folder (§2.1.d).
  • All asset paths are under 150 characters (§2.1.e).
  • No executables, DLLs, .apk, .app or archives that hide content (§1.5.a, §2.2.a).
  • No watermarks, DRM, time limits or feature locks (§1.4.b).
  • The package does not phone home, proxy traffic or collect analytics (§1.1.g, §1.5.e).

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Every script is inside the ChosenOfTheHarvest namespace (§2.5.a).
  • Editor menus are under Tools → Chosen of the Harvest (§2.5.1.a).
  • No reflection into Unity Editor internal APIs (§2.5.g).
  • No obsolete or deprecated API warnings on the target Unity version (§2.5.i).
  • Fast Enter Playmode works with Domain Reload disabled (§2.5.h — mandatory from Unity 6.6). Every static field is reset in a [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(SubsystemRegistration)] method.

docs.title: Verifying a build
docs.text:
.\Tools\build.ps1 -RunSmoke

What happens:

  1. Unity builds Build/ChosenOfTheHarvest.exe.
  2. The script launches it with -smoke.
  3. SmokeTest.cs drives the game: audio, weapons, dodge, damage, building, production, hauling, companions, needs, beds, jobs, menus, inventory, catalog, repairs, interiors, quests, campaign, floor plans, combat, elites, shops, puzzles, curses, bosses, omens, descent, victory, meta, ceremonies, save/load, pause and localisation.

BuildLogs/SMOKE_LOG.txt
%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\ChosenOfTheHarvest\ChosenOfTheHarvest\Player.log

docs.text:
A Windows development build is roughly 180 MB, dominated by UnityPlayer.dll and the Mono runtime. The package you submit to the Asset Store is the project, not the build; the project's Assets folder is about 43 MB.

Never submit a build

The Asset Store does not accept executables inside a package. Do not include Build/, Library/, Logs/, BuildLogs/ or UserSettings/ in a submission.

• The build is deterministic enough for CI; the smoke test is the regression gate.
  • Run Unity with -batchmode -quit -nographics for headless machines.
  • The editor writes its licence state to the machine; a CI runner needs a licensed Unity install or a Unity licence server.

docs.title: Catalogs API reference
docs.text: Every number the player can feel — weapon rhythm, rite damage, heirloom bonuses, armour effects, companion traits, building costs — lives in a static catalog class rather than in the systems that use them.

docs.title: How the catalogs work
docs.text:
• A catalog is a public static class with readonly entries and a Get(id) lookup; entries are plain C# objects, not ScriptableObjects.
  • The equipped identity is a string id on HarvestSaveData (weaponType, riteType, armorId, charmId), resolved through the catalog on demand.
  • Unknown ids never throw: weapons and rites fall back to the first entry, heirlooms and attire to null.
  • Because HarvestState computes bonuses from the same ids, adding an entry requires adding its effect in GameState.cs; the table alone is not enough.

docs.title: Dungeon API reference
docs.text:
Expedition builds and runs a pilgrimage floor one room at a time: it generates a room graph, dresses a single room, spawns husks, traps and the act's Warden, then opens the doors when the room is cleared. Everything below lives in the single ChosenOfTheHarvest namespace and is created at runtime — no prefabs to wire.

File names and class names differ

The files are named after the feature, not the type they contain. Search for the class: Dungeon.cs holds Expedition, Enemy.cs holds Creature, BossController.cs holds WardenController, BossArena.cs holds WardenArena, DungeonTrap.cs holds ExpeditionTrap, PressurePlate.cs holds RunePlate, Projectile.cs holds HexBolt, and FloorPlan.cs holds FloorPlanGenerator.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Expedition owns the floor and builds rooms; FloorPlanGenerator decides the graph; Creature and WardenController fight; WardenArena dresses the boss room; ExpeditionTrap, RunePlate and HexBolt are the small MonoBehaviour props; and RoomCollision provides XZ bounds and pillar collision without Unity physics.

docs.text:
Builds a fully connected grid, promotes one room per role, then locks a few side edges.

The grid is 5 × 2 for act 0, 8 × 2 for act 1 and 5 × 4 for act 2 — 10, 16 and 20 rooms per floor, 92 rooms across three acts with two floors each. Every floor promotes shop, treasure, curse, puzzle, rescue and forge once, adds 1 + act elite rooms (plus a second treasure room from act 2), and locks 2 + act edges; rooms 0 and the Warden room are never lock endpoints.

docs.title: ExpeditionTrap
docs.text:
A glowing circle that telegraphs for 0.75 s, then damages anything inside. Spawn(Transform parent, Transform playerTarget, Vector3 ground, float trapRadius, int trapDamage) creates an inactive trap with a random 1.2–2.2 s first cooldown.

Damage lands when the player is within radius + 0.25 at the end of the telegraph, then the cooldown rerolls to 1.6–2.6 s. Combat rooms spawn 2 traps and elite rooms 3, with damage 8 + pilgrimages and radius 0.95–1.25 — see Expedition.SpawnTraps.

docs.title: RunePlate
docs.text: One plate of the three-rune puzzle. Spawn(Expedition owner, Transform parent, Vector3 ground, int index) creates it and pulses it until the sovereign comes within 0.8 units, then it turns green, plays pickup, and calls owner.ActivateRune(this) exactly once.

docs.title: HexBolt
docs.text:
Pooled enemy projectile — a camera-facing sprite that travels on the ground plane. Spawn(Vector3 position, Vector3 direction, int damage, Color tint, float speed = 5.5f) reuses an inactive bolt, or creates one while the pool is under 48.

Bolts live 4 s, despawn on room geometry (RoomCollision.IsFree at radius 0.12), and hit the sovereign within 0.6 units for damage. Creature.CastAtPlayer and WardenController fan/radial attacks are the only callers.

Expedition.SpawnCreature derives everything from the archetype. With d = HarvestState.Data.pilgrimages and f = Floor - 1:

docs.text:
EliteModifier has None plus the three below. Elites are picked as (index + ActIndex) % 3 + 1 and already carry ×1.5 health, ×1.3 damage, ×1.08 scale and a 35 % blend towards amber before the modifier lands.

Modifier Effect Verified in Armored DamageReduction raised to at least 0.3 (30 % less damage taken) ApplyElite Frenzied SpeedMultiplier *= 1.25, AttackCooldown *= 0.8 ApplyElite Vampiric Melee hits heal the husk for 30 % of its Damage MeleeRoutine

docs.text:
Layered on top of the boss Creature; the creature still walks, takes damage and dies through the normal path.

Phase two begins automatically at 50 % health. Routines lock movement, telegraph, then deal damage and release:

docs.title: Warden roster
docs.text:
Three Wardens, one per act, two floors each. The second floor is the Ascendant form — the same name with " Ascendant" appended and tougher stats.

docs.title: Followers API reference
docs.text: Companions are runtime CompanionAgent objects bound to a persistent CompanionRecord: the record survives save/load, the agent does the walking, working and socialising. This page documents both, the job/bed/priority plumbing they share with Sanctum, and the two small helpers that make the hub readable — NavGrid for pathing and CompanionNameTag for billboarded names.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
CompanionAgent is the brain and body, CompanionRecord is the save data, CompanionCatalog supplies names/traits/tints, NavGrid is a grid A* over the hub, and CompanionNameTag is the floating label. All five live in the ChosenOfTheHarvest namespace.

Records are index-aligned with agents

HarvestState.CompanionAt(index) and HarvestGame.Companions[index] describe the same companion. SpawnCompanion binds them in order, and friendship/partnership fields store those indices, so never reorder the companion list without a save migration.

docs.title: Mode and the decision loop
docs.text:
Mode has twelve values; the agent re-decides every 0.8 s.

Mode Entered by Left when Wander Default, dissent, illness, no job A higher rule applies Attend Attend (cutscenes, ceremonies) Explicitly re-tasked Work WorkAt, WanderHome, wake-up Night, dissent, illness, no job Sleep Night with a bed, exhaustion ≥ 85 Not night and exhaustion < 30, or ≤ 4 Eat Hunger < 25 with food in store Reaches FoodSpot Rest Night without a bed, exhaustion, RestNow Exhaustion < 20 or the rest timer expires Haul Job store full at the work spot Reaches HaulSpot Clean No job and a shrine with Dirt > 25 Dirt ≤ 4 Reflection EnterReflection Loyalty ≥ 45 or 40 s of reflection Repair No job and a sanctum with Condition < 60 Condition ≥ 99.5 Social Dusk with priority 2 and a Tea House Dusk ends, sick, dissenting Pray Dusk with priority 1 and a Shrine Dusk ends, sick, dissenting

The order below is the verified order in Decide(); the first match wins.

  1. Reflection releases at loyalty ≥ 45 or after 40 s.
  2. Social/Pray drop to Wander outside dusk, or when sick or dissenting.
  3. Sleep wakes outside night once exhaustion < 30, or at ≤ 4.
  4. Rest wakes at exhaustion < 20 or when its timer runs out.
  5. Eat and Haul make no decisions until they arrive.
  6. Night: Sleep if a bed is assigned, otherwise Rest.
  7. Exhaustion ≥ 85 with a bed forces Sleep even by day.
  8. Hunger < 25 with food available sends the agent to Eat.
  9. Dissenters and the sick are forced to Wander.
  10. Dusk plus priority 2 sends them to the nearest Tea House (Social); priority 1 to the nearest Shrine (Pray).
  11. Unfinished Clean/Repair continue while the target still needs work.
  12. With no job: the nearest dirty shrine, then the nearest damaged sanctum.
  13. With a job: Work at Job.WorkSpot.
  14. Otherwise: Wander around home.

docs.title: Needs, sickness and loyalty
docs.text:
TickNeeds runs only while input is unlocked, so pausing the game does not starve anyone. All rates are per real second.

Need Rate Hunger −0.30 base; Glutton ×1.5, austerity creed ×0.8, sick ×1.1, asleep ×0.3, reflecting ×0.55 Starvation 45 s at zero hunger calls HarvestGame.CompanionDied Exhaustion +0.10 awake (Lazy 0.15), ×1.35 sick; −3.2 asleep or resting, −0.9 reflecting Loyalty −0.065 while suffering, otherwise +0.012; the Loyal trait scales the rate ×0.6 Social mode +0.04 loyalty while socialising

Suffering means hunger < 25, illness, or exhaustion > 90. On top of that, standing inside a sanctum aura trickles loyalty: Shrine 0.018, Temple 0.02, Bell Tower 0.018, Obelisk 0.015, Tea House 0.01, Sun Bath 0.01 (and −0.08 exhaustion), Reliquary 0.01, plus 0.012 × InteriorAuraBonus for built interiors.

Mood is a cascade: Dissenting (< 20 loyalty), Ill, Starving (< 20 hunger), Exhausted (> 80), Sleeping, Hungry (< 45), Tired (> 60), Devoted (> 85), then Content.

Illness is rolled every 12 s: 35 % chance for Sickly and 8 % otherwise, but only while hunger < 25 or exhaustion > 85. Recovery needs hunger > 60, exhaustion < 35, at least 18 s ill, and a small per-frame roll. Work grants 1 XP per second, levels cap at 5, and each level gives +4 loyalty.

docs.title: Jobs, beds and priorities
docs.text:
WorkAt claims the sanctum's single Worker slot and releases the previous one; AssignBed does the same for Sleeper. Companions touch only these Sanctum members (see Scripts/Buildings/Building.cs):

Member Type Description Worker, Sleeper, Penitent CompanionAgent Exclusive occupants WorkSpot, SleepSpot, ReflectionSpot Vector3 Offsets from the building IsReflection bool True for the Reflection Chamber Type SanctumType Aura, job and priority rules key off this Stored int Produced units waiting for a haul Dirt, Condition float Cleaning and repair thresholds TakeStored() int Removes and returns the stored units

While working, an agent hauls as soon as the store reaches 4 units (2 for a Herb Garden), carrying them to HarvestGame.HaulSpot. Priorities change daily life, not the work loop: priority 1 adds +1 grace every 20 s, priority 2 socialises harder at dusk. HarvestGame.RecruitCompanion refuses at 30 companions, and HarvestGame.CompanionDied removes the agent and leaves a memorial.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: Friendship is attempted every 12 s with a Tea House (18 s without) for companions who are not sleeping, reflecting, or already paired: both must be within 5 units (3 without a Tea House), then both gain +4 loyalty and each records the other. Romance is attempted every 30 s and needs both sides at age ≥ 18, loyalty ≥ 80 and level ≥ 2, plus an 18 % roll; success grants +10 loyalty each. EnterReflection gives dissenters a route back: they leave their job, sit in the chamber, and exit reformed at loyalty 45 or after 40 s.

docs.title: NavGrid
docs.text:
Static grid A* over the hub. Begin allocates the grid, Mark blocks scenery, FindPath returns a corner-clipped path or null.

Member Returns Description Ready bool True between Begin and Clear Begin(Vector2 halfBounds, float cell = 1f) void Allocates the grid; cell size is clamped to ≥ 0.5 Mark(Vector3 world, float radius) void Blocks every cell within radius + 0.42 End() void Leaves Ready set — it does not post-process the grid Clear() void Drops the grid and clears Ready FindPath(Vector3 from, Vector3 to) Vector3[] Cell centres excluding the start cell; null if unreachable

Paths are 8-directional with diagonal corner-cutting disallowed, use the octile heuristic, and snap a blocked goal to the nearest free cell within 4 cells. Agents repath at most every 0.9 s and fall back to a straight line when Ready is false, then clamp themselves to HarvestGame.Instance.Player.Bounds.

docs.title: CompanionNameTag
docs.text:
Create(Transform parent, Transform target, string text, Color tint) builds a TextMesh label 2.35 units above the target. LateUpdate copies the main camera's rotation, scales with distance (clamped 0.9–1.2), renders at sorting order 5000, and destroys itself if the target disappears.

var boot = HarvestGame.Instance;
var companion = boot.Companions[0];

// Point the first companion at a shrine job and a bed, then read its state.
Sanctum shrine = null, bed = null;
foreach (var sanctum in boot.Sanctums)
{
    if (sanctum.Type == SanctumType.Shrine) shrine = sanctum;
    else if (sanctum.Type == SanctumType.Bed) bed = sanctum;
}

if (shrine != null) companion.AssignJob(shrine);
if (bed != null) companion.AssignBed(bed);
companion.SetPriority(1);            // 0 work, 1 grace, 2 social

Debug.Log(companion.StatusLine);     // mood, trait, job, H/L/E
Debug.Log(companion.Mood + " / " + companion.PriorityName);

Testing the loop

HarvestGame.Companions is a read-only list, so a test can walk every agent, force SetPriority, Feed or RestNow, and log CurrentMode. The built-in smoke test does exactly this before it exercises the companion menu.

docs.title: Localisation key reference
docs.text: Every player-facing string in the template is addressed by a dotted key and resolved through the Lexicon static class from a JSON table in Assets/ChosenOfTheHarvest/Resources/Localization. This page documents the key convention, lists all 349 English keys grouped by prefix, and explains the ?XX?-prefixed pseudo-locale used for layout testing.

docs.title: How Lexicon resolves a string
Key naming convention
docs.text:
Rule Example <system>.<subject>[.<detail>], lowercase, dot separated quest.hymn, trait.lazy.desc Compound subjects are concatenated, never hyphenated dungeon.treasuretaken, menu.actions.reflection Screen and menu titles are ALL CAPS campaign.title, shop.sell.title Toast keys mirror the action that produced them companion.blessed, slots.deleted Input prompts are prefixed with the key glyph [E] Descend deeper, [B] Build Fields are separated by a spaced bullet • ACT I • ASHEN ORCHARD • The Gilded Stag Placeholders are positional {0}–{3}, filled by Lexicon.Format shop.heirloom = {0} • 25 pearls • stock {1} Ellipses are three ASCII dots, never … The rose garden is growing...

Four prefixes are composed at runtime from an enum name, so the key is never a literal in code:

Composed key Source Values building.<type> Sanctum.Label, type.ToString().ToLowerInvariant() 20 building names room.<type> FloorPlanGenerator.Name(type) entrance … forge trait.<trait> / trait.<trait>.desc CompanionCatalog 6 traits × 2 phase.<phase> SeasonCycle.PhaseName dawn, day, dusk, night

campaign.act1–campaign.act3 sit in a fixed array, and quest.* / npc.hint.* are referenced from ordered lists in QuestSystem and HarvestGame, so their key names are positional: reordering those lists reorders the story.

docs.title: The pseudo-locale
docs.text:
xx.json is a layout test, not a translation: it has the same 349 keys in the same order, and every value is the English text prefixed with the literal ASCII marker ?XX?.

{
  "entries": [
    { "key": "title.name", "value": "?XX? CHOSEN OF THE HARVEST" },
    { "key": "dungeon.runes", "value": "?XX? Runes {0}/{1}" }
  ]
}

Because the marker is plain ASCII it renders in any font, so a missing glyph shows up immediately, and {0} placeholders survive so Format calls still exercise their arguments. Two ways to use it:

  • In the build: Preferences → page 2 → Language switches English ⇄ Pseudo (layout) at runtime.
  • In the smoke test: SmokeTest switches to xx, formats hud.day, and logs SMOKE locale pseudo=… keys=349 before switching back — the fastest way to catch a table that failed to load.

Add a real locale

  1. Copy en.json to <code>.json (for example de.json) in Resources/Localization.
  2. Keep every key string byte-identical and keep the {0}–{3} placeholders in the translated values.
  3. Keep layout-bearing spacing in hud.* and the • separators.
  4. Switch with Lexicon.SetLocale("de"), then confirm Lexicon.KeyCount matches 349.
  5. If the table fails to parse, Lexicon logs Lexicon table failed to load: … and falls back to code defaults.
